playbooks.title: Low fuel pressure / fuel pump delivery and control
playbooks.summary: Low fuel system pressure and fuel pump circuit codes are diagnosed by first comparing desired and actual fuel pressure in scan data, then separating supply problems (weak pump, restricted filter, leaking regulator) from pump control and circuit problems (relay, pump control module, wiring, grounds) and pressure sensor faults. Confirm with a gauge, volume test, and loaded voltage drop test before replacing a pump. On direct-injection engines, first decide whether the shortfall is on the low-pressure supply side or the high-pressure side.
clarifyingQuestions: Is the engine port injected, direct injected, or dual injection, and is the fuel system return-type or returnless?
Does the problem occur mainly under load (acceleration, uphill, towing), when the engine is hot, or at low fuel level?
Is the fault intermittent (engine cuts out and recovers) or constant?
Has the vehicle recently been refueled, run out of fuel, or had fuel system, rear body, or collision repairs?
Are fuel pump control or pump module codes stored in the PCM or in other modules?

causes.title: Weak or failing in-tank fuel pump
causes.description: A worn pump (commutator/brush wear, worn impeller) cannot maintain pressure or volume when flow demand rises, producing low pressure under load, loss of power, and stalling; a leaking pump check valve causes long cranking after the vehicle sits.

modifiers.reason: Low fuel rail/system pressure code present
Pressure sensor circuit codes point toward the sensor circuit rather than the pump
Worn pumps often lose output when hot
Flow demand is highest under load

causes.title: Restricted fuel filter or pump inlet strainer
causes.description: A clogged filter or in-tank strainer limits flow, so pressure may look acceptable at idle but falls when flow demand rises. Contaminated fuel or tank debris accelerates restriction.

modifiers.reason: Restriction shows up at high flow
Filters and strainers load up with age

causes.title: Faulty fuel pressure regulator
causes.description: A regulator that sticks open or has a weak spring bypasses fuel and lowers system pressure; on return-type systems a ruptured diaphragm can also draw fuel into the vacuum reference hose. On returnless systems the regulator is usually part of the in-tank module.

modifiers.reason: A leaking diaphragm can cause rich running and fuel odor

causes.title: Fuel pump relay or fuse circuit fault
causes.description: Burned relay contacts or a failing relay coil cause intermittent or reduced pump voltage, leading to stalling, no-start, or low pressure. Applies to relay-controlled pump systems.

modifiers.reason: Fuel pump primary/secondary circuit code present

causes.title: Fuel pump control (driver) module fault
causes.description: On systems that vary pump speed through a separate pump control module, a failed module or its connector produces low, erratic, or no pump output and commonly sets pump control circuit codes. Some modules are mounted where they are exposed to moisture and road salt.

modifiers.reason: Fuel pump control circuit code present
Moisture exposure accelerates module and connector failure

causes.title: Fuel pump feed, control, or sensor wiring damage
causes.description: Chafed, pinched, or poorly repaired wiring between the relay or control module and the pump, in the PCM control lines, or in the pressure sensor circuit adds resistance or opens intermittently, reducing pump output or corrupting the pressure signal.

modifiers.reason: Pump circuit or control circuit code present

causes.title: Corroded or overheated pump, module, or sensor connector
causes.description: High resistance at the fuel pump module connector, tank pass-through, pump control module, or pressure sensor connector reduces pump voltage or distorts the sensor signal; overheated terminals may be discolored or melted.

modifiers.reason: Pump circuit or control circuit code present
Terminal fretting and corrosion increase with age

causes.title: Poor fuel pump or pump control module ground
causes.description: A loose or corroded ground at the pump, tank, chassis, or control module reduces effective pump voltage exactly like a feed-side resistance, so pressure sags as current demand rises.

modifiers.reason: Pump circuit or control circuit code present

causes.title: Fuel rail pressure sensor fault
causes.description: A skewed, stuck, or intermittent pressure sensor makes the PCM see pressure that is not really there (or miss pressure that is), setting pressure or sensor codes and causing incorrect pump commands.

modifiers.reason: Fuel rail pressure sensor circuit code present

causes.title: High-pressure fuel pump (direct-injection engines)
causes.description: On direct-injection engines, low rail pressure is often a high-side problem: a worn high-pressure pump, its metering valve, or its drive fails to build rail pressure even with a healthy low-pressure supply. Not applicable to port-injection-only engines.

tests.title: Compare desired vs actual fuel pressure PIDs
tests.purpose: Use scan data to see whether actual fuel pressure follows the PCM's desired value and whether the pressure reading itself is plausible.
procedure: Record all DTCs from all modules and the freeze frame data; note load, RPM, fuel level, and temperatures when the code set.
Identify the fuel system type (return or returnless, port or direct injection) from service information and confirm which fuel pressure and pump command PIDs the vehicle supports.
Key on, engine off: watch the pressure PID during pump prime; it should rise promptly when the pump runs.
Start the engine and record desired and actual pressure (and pump command or duty cycle, if available) at idle.
Perform a snap throttle and, where safe, a road test under the freeze-frame load conditions while graphing desired vs actual.
Note whether actual lags desired, drops under load, stays low at all times, or reads implausibly (stuck, erratic, or not responding to prime or start).
tools: Scan tool with fuel pressure and pump command PIDs
Service information for fuel system type and PID behavior
tests.expected: Actual fuel pressure closely follows desired at prime, idle, snap throttle, and under load, and the pump command is not at its maximum; values are within the OEM specification.
tests.specNote: Desired/actual pressure ranges and pump command limits per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Actual pressure tracks desired under all conditions
outcomes.interpretation: Delivery is adequate right now. Intermittent electrical causes (relay, module, wiring, connectors) remain possible; reproduce the freeze-frame conditions or move to circuit tests if pump control codes are present.

outcomes.label: Adequate at idle but falls below desired under load or snap throttle
outcomes.interpretation: Supply cannot keep up with demand, typical of a weak pump, a restricted filter or strainer, or voltage loss in the pump circuit. Confirm with a gauge or volume test and a loaded voltage drop test.

outcomes.label: Below desired at idle and under load, or pump command at maximum
outcomes.interpretation: Pressure is low even at low flow: a leaking regulator, a badly worn pump, or reduced pump voltage or control are likely. Verify with a mechanical gauge before condemning parts.

outcomes.label: Pressure reading is implausible (stuck, erratic, or not responding to prime or start)
outcomes.interpretation: The pressure sensor or its circuit is suspect. Compare against a mechanical gauge and test the sensor reference, ground, and signal circuits.

outcomes.label: No fuel pressure PID available on this vehicle
outcomes.interpretation: Systems without a pressure sensor need a mechanical gauge test.

tests.title: Visual inspection of fuel lines, pump connector, and pump control wiring
tests.purpose: Find obvious damage such as leaks, kinked lines, overheated connectors, or corroded modules before deeper testing.
procedure: With the engine off, inspect accessible fuel lines and fittings for leaks, kinks, crush damage, or non-OEM repairs.
Safely raise and support the vehicle on a lift or jack stands and inspect the tank area, serviceable filter (if equipped), and lines along the frame.
Inspect the fuel pump module connector (through the access panel or at the top of the tank where accessible) for discolored, melted, or corroded terminals.
Locate the fuel pump relay, fuse, and any pump control module; inspect for corrosion, water intrusion, loose mounting, or overheated terminals.
Check the pump and control module ground connections for looseness or corrosion.
If contamination is suspected, draw a fuel sample into a clear approved container and check for water, debris, or unusual color or odor.
tools: Lift or jack and jack stands
tests.expected: No leaks, restrictions, or damaged, overheated, or corroded wiring and connectors; the fuel sample is clear with no water or debris.

outcomes.label: No visible faults found
outcomes.interpretation: No obvious fault; continue with pressure, electrical, and flow testing.

outcomes.label: Damaged, overheated, or corroded wiring, connectors, grounds, or module found
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the damaged circuit and retest under load. An overheated pump connector can also be caused by a pump drawing excessive current, so check pump current after the repair.

outcomes.label: Kinked or restricted line, fuel leak, or contaminated fuel found
outcomes.interpretation: Correct the restriction, leak, or contaminated fuel, then retest pressure and volume. A fuel leak is a fire hazard; do not operate the vehicle until it is repaired.

tests.title: Check TSBs and open recalls for the fuel pump, pump control, and software
tests.purpose: Fuel pumps, pump control modules, and pump control software are frequent subjects of recalls and service bulletins.
procedure: Enter the VIN in the OEM service portal or a professional information system and list open recalls.
Search bulletins by the DTCs present and by the symptom (hard start, stall, loss of power).
Compare bulletin conditions (build dates, engine, symptoms, freeze-frame conditions) with this vehicle.
Note any required software update, revised part, or bulletin-specific diagnostic steps.
tools: OEM service portal or professional information system
tests.expected: No applicable open recall or bulletin, or the bulletin's diagnostic steps are followed before any parts replacement.

outcomes.label: Applicable recall or TSB for the fuel pump or pump module (low or high pressure)
outcomes.interpretation: Follow the bulletin's diagnostic procedure to confirm the condition before replacing parts; recalls must be performed by an authorized dealer.

outcomes.label: Applicable recall or TSB for the pump control module, wiring or connector, or pump control software
outcomes.interpretation: Perform the bulletin's inspection or software update, then retest before replacing the pump.

outcomes.label: No applicable bulletin or recall
outcomes.interpretation: Continue with standard diagnosis.

tests.title: Command the fuel pump and verify relay / pump control module operation
tests.purpose: Determine whether the pump receives power when commanded and, if not, where the command chain breaks.
procedure: Using the scan tool output control (or the OEM key-on prime strategy), command the fuel pump on and listen at the filler neck or tank for pump operation.
On relay-controlled systems, verify the relay coil is energized and the switched output reaches the pump feed; substitute a known-good identical relay if needed.
On module-controlled systems, verify the PCM command signal arrives at the pump control module and that the module output changes with the command (use a lab scope for pulse-width-modulated outputs).
Review pump control module DTCs, communication codes, and any feedback or diagnostic signal to the PCM.
Wiggle the harness at the relay, control module, and tank connectors while the pump is commanded to expose intermittent opens.
tools: Scan tool with fuel pump output control
tests.expected: The pump runs whenever commanded; relay or control module output follows the command, and the wiggle test causes no dropout.
tests.specNote: Pump control strategy (relay or PWM module, command and duty cycle ranges) per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Pump runs whenever commanded; outputs follow the command
outcomes.interpretation: The command chain works at present; focus on pump output, restriction, and loaded voltage drop.

outcomes.label: Relay coil energized but no switched output, or a known-good relay restores operation
outcomes.interpretation: The relay is implicated. Inspect the relay socket terminals for heat damage before installing a new relay.

outcomes.label: Valid command reaches the pump control module but its output is missing or does not follow the command
outcomes.interpretation: Verify the module's power and ground under load; if they are good, the pump control module is the likely fault.

outcomes.label: Command signal missing at the relay or module, or dropout during the wiggle test
outcomes.interpretation: Trace the control circuit between the PCM and the relay or module for opens, shorts, or connector faults. If the circuit is intact and the PCM still does not command the pump, follow the OEM PCM output diagnostics (PCM driver faults are uncommon).

outcomes.label: Output control not supported and pump prime could not be observed
outcomes.interpretation: Check for power at the pump connector during key-on prime with a DVOM or test light instead.

tests.title: Loaded voltage drop test of the fuel pump power and ground circuits
tests.purpose: Find resistance in the pump feed or ground that reduces pump speed; such faults are missed by unloaded ohmmeter checks.
procedure: Back-probe the pump connector (or the nearest accessible point) without damaging terminal seals; do not pierce wiring insulation.
With the pump running (engine running or pump commanded on), measure voltage between the battery positive post and the pump feed terminal.
With the pump running, measure voltage between the pump ground terminal and the battery negative post.
Measure the voltage available directly across the pump terminals and compare it with battery voltage.
If a drop is excessive, split the circuit at the relay or module output, inline connectors, and ground points to locate the resistance.
tests.expected: Voltage drop on each side of the circuit is small, commonly a few tenths of a volt or less (general guideline — verify against OEM specification), and the pump receives nearly full system voltage.

outcomes.label: Feed and ground voltage drops within limits
outcomes.interpretation: The pump is receiving full voltage; if pressure or volume is low, the pump, filter, or regulator is the likely cause.

outcomes.label: Excessive voltage drop on the power feed side
outcomes.interpretation: Split the feed circuit (relay or module output, fuse, inline and tank connectors) to find the resistance, repair it, and retest pump output.

outcomes.label: Excessive voltage drop on the ground side
outcomes.interpretation: Clean and secure the ground connection or repair the ground wire, then retest.

outcomes.label: No voltage at the pump when commanded
outcomes.interpretation: Check fuses, relay or module output, and any crash or inertia fuel shutoff (where equipped). A pump that repeatedly blows its fuse may be drawing excessive current; check pump current.

outcomes.label: Intermittent fault not present during testing
outcomes.interpretation: Repeat the test while reproducing the freeze-frame conditions or while wiggling the harness.

tests.title: Fuel pump current waveform with a low-amp probe
tests.purpose: Evaluate pump motor condition and circuit health without opening the fuel system by viewing pump current on a lab scope.
procedure: Clamp a low-amp current probe around the pump feed or ground wire, or use a fused jumper loop at the relay socket.
Run the pump (engine running or commanded on) and capture several seconds of current waveform.
Compare average current with OEM or known-good reference data for this pump and check the regularity of the commutator segment humps.
Repeat at the freeze-frame operating condition if possible.
tools: Known-good waveform library or OEM data
tests.expected: Steady average current typical for this pump (per OEM or known-good reference data) with regular, repeating commutator humps and no dropouts.
tests.specNote: Pump current varies with pump design; use OEM data or a known-good comparison.

outcomes.label: Current and waveform shape normal
outcomes.interpretation: The pump motor appears healthy; look at restriction, regulation, or the pressure reading itself.

outcomes.label: Irregular or missing commutator humps, or current dropouts
outcomes.interpretation: Worn commutator segments or brushes are indicated. Rule out an intermittent connection with a wiggle test, then confirm low output with a pressure or volume test.

outcomes.label: Average current higher than expected
outcomes.interpretation: The pump is working hard: suspect a restriction (filter, strainer, pinched line) or a binding pump.

outcomes.label: Average current lower than expected
outcomes.interpretation: Suspect resistance in the pump circuit (confirm with a loaded voltage drop test) or a regulator bypassing fuel so the pump is lightly loaded.

tests.title: Mechanical fuel pressure gauge test: prime, idle, load, and leak-down
tests.purpose: Measure actual low-side fuel pressure independently of the PCM sensor and check pressure hold after shutdown.
procedure: Relieve fuel system pressure per the OEM procedure. Keep a fire extinguisher nearby, work in a ventilated area away from ignition sources, and wear eye protection.

Connect a gauge rated for the system to the low-pressure test port or with the correct adapter. On direct-injection engines connect only to the low-pressure supply side; never connect a gauge to the high-pressure rail.
Cycle the key to prime and check the gauge connection for leaks before starting the engine.
Record pressure at key-on prime, idle, and snap throttle, and compare with the scan tool pressure PID (if equipped) at the same moments.
If the complaint occurs under load, use a pressure transducer and lab scope or a gauge mounted outside the passenger compartment; never route a pressurized fuel hose into the cabin.
Shut the engine off and record pressure hold over the time specified by the OEM.
Relieve pressure, remove the gauge, reinstall the test port cap, and check for leaks with the system pressurized.
tools: Fuel pressure gauge kit with correct adapters
Approved fuel container and shop towels
tests.expected: Pressure reaches and holds the OEM specification at prime, idle, and under load, agrees with the PCM pressure PID, and holds for the specified time after shutdown.
tests.specNote: Pressure specifications, test port location, and hold time per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Pressure within specification in all conditions and agrees with the PID
outcomes.interpretation: Low-side delivery is good at present. Suspect an intermittent electrical fault or, on direct-injection engines, the high-pressure side.

outcomes.label: Gauge pressure within specification but the PCM pressure PID reads differently
outcomes.interpretation: The pressure sensor or its circuit is misreporting. Test the sensor reference, ground, and signal before replacing the sensor.

outcomes.label: Pressure low at prime and idle
outcomes.interpretation: Check pump voltage under load first; with good voltage, isolate the regulator from the pump per the OEM procedure.

outcomes.label: Pressure normal at idle but drops under load or snap throttle
outcomes.interpretation: Flow cannot meet demand: perform a volume test and a loaded voltage drop test to separate restriction, pump wear, and circuit resistance.

outcomes.label: Pressure bleeds down quickly after shutdown
outcomes.interpretation: Isolate the leak path per the OEM procedure: a leaking regulator, pump check valve, or injector can cause bleed-down. A leaking injector also causes flooding and long cranking.

outcomes.label: No accessible test port or adapter available
outcomes.interpretation: Use the pressure PID, a volume test, or an OEM-approved adapter.

tests.title: Fuel volume (flow) test
tests.purpose: Pressure alone can look acceptable with a weak or restricted supply; delivered volume shows whether the pump and filter can meet demand.
procedure: Relieve fuel pressure per the OEM procedure and observe fire precautions: extinguisher at hand, ventilation, no ignition sources, eye protection.
Connect a flow meter inline, or route the OEM-specified test point into a graduated approved fuel container as described in service information.
Run the pump for the specified time (commanded on or per the OEM method) and measure delivered volume while monitoring pump voltage.
Compare delivered volume with the OEM specification and note air bubbles or debris in the sample.
Reconnect all lines, pressurize the system, and inspect every disturbed connection for leaks.
tools: Fuel flow meter or graduated approved fuel container
tests.expected: Delivered volume meets or exceeds the OEM specification with the pump at full available voltage; fuel is clean and free of air bubbles.
tests.specNote: Volume/flow specification and test method per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Delivered volume meets specification
outcomes.interpretation: Supply capacity is adequate. If pressure was low, suspect the regulator; if pressure was normal, look at the sensor or high-pressure side.

outcomes.label: Delivered volume below specification
outcomes.interpretation: If pump voltage was normal during the test, a weak pump or restricted filter or strainer is indicated; service a replaceable filter first and retest. If pump voltage was low, repair the circuit and retest before condemning the pump.

outcomes.label: No safe test point available
outcomes.interpretation: Rely on loaded pressure testing and pump current analysis.

tests.title: Fuel rail pressure sensor reference, ground, and signal circuit test
tests.purpose: Separate a failed pressure sensor from wiring, connector, or ground faults when sensor codes are set or the PID is implausible.
procedure: Key off: inspect the sensor connector for corrosion, fuel intrusion, pushed-out terminals, and damaged seals.
Key on, engine off: back-probe and measure the reference voltage and the sensor ground (voltage drop to battery negative) at the sensor connector.
Measure the signal voltage and compare it with the scan tool reading; with the engine running, confirm the signal changes smoothly with pressure.
Wiggle-test the harness from the sensor to the PCM while watching the signal on a lab scope or graphing meter for dropouts.
If the reference is low, check whether other sensors share it; disconnecting them one at a time can reveal a shorted sensor pulling the reference down.
tests.expected: Reference and ground are within the OEM specification; the signal matches the scan tool, changes smoothly with pressure, and does not drop out during the wiggle test.
tests.specNote: Reference voltage, signal range, and allowable ground drop per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Reference, ground, and signal all good
outcomes.interpretation: The sensor circuit is sound; a pressure code is more likely caused by actual pressure problems.

outcomes.label: Reference voltage missing or low, or excessive ground drop
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the reference or ground circuit. If the reference recovers when a sensor is unplugged, that sensor is shorted internally.

outcomes.label: Reference and ground good but the signal is stuck, out of range, or drops out
outcomes.interpretation: With good reference and ground, a stuck or skewed signal indicates the sensor; check the signal wire for opens or shorts first. Some sensors are not serviced separately from the rail; follow the OEM procedure.

outcomes.label: Could not reproduce the fault
outcomes.interpretation: Monitor the signal during a road test or while reproducing freeze-frame conditions.

tests.title: Direct injection: compare low-side supply and high-side rail pressure PIDs
tests.purpose: On direct-injection engines, decide whether low pressure originates in the low-pressure supply or on the high-pressure pump side.
procedure: Confirm from service information that the engine is direct injected and identify the PIDs for low-side (supply) and high-side (rail) pressure.
At idle, record desired and actual values for both the low-side and high-side pressures.
Perform a snap throttle and a loaded road test under the freeze-frame conditions while graphing both desired vs actual pairs.
Note which side falls behind first: a low-side shortfall starves the high-pressure pump, while a high-side shortfall with good supply points at the high-pressure side.
Do not open any part of the high-pressure system for this test.
tools: Scan tool with low-side and high-side fuel pressure PIDs
tests.expected: Low-side and high-side actual pressures both track their desired values under all conditions.

outcomes.label: Low-side and high-side pressures both track desired
outcomes.interpretation: No pressure shortfall at present; the fault may be intermittent or electrical.

outcomes.label: Low-side (supply) pressure falls below desired
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the low-pressure supply first; a starved high-pressure pump cannot hold rail pressure.

outcomes.label: Low side tracks, but high-side rail pressure falls below desired
outcomes.interpretation: The high-pressure side is implicated (pump, metering valve, drive, rail sensor, or relief valve); continue with the direct-injection high-pressure diagnostics.

outcomes.label: Engine is port injected only
outcomes.interpretation: Test not applicable.

verification: Record freeze frame data, then clear DTCs.
Confirm actual fuel pressure tracks desired at prime, idle, snap throttle, and under road load, and is within the OEM specification on a gauge where applicable.
Road test under the freeze-frame conditions (load, temperature, fuel level) and confirm the fuel pressure monitor runs and passes with no DTC returning.
With the system pressurized, inspect every disturbed fuel fitting and connector for leaks before releasing the vehicle.

playbooks.title: Direct injection high-pressure fuel system (pump, regulator control, rail pressure sensor)
playbooks.summary: Direct-injection pressure faults are diagnosed by graphing rail pressure desired vs actual together with the high-pressure pump control command, then confirming the low-pressure supply before blaming the high-pressure pump. Validate the rail pressure sensor and pump control circuit, check for injector leakage and software updates, and inspect the pump drive where applicable. The high-pressure side is extremely dangerous: it can hold very high pressure after shutdown, and a leak can inject fuel through skin, so never open it without the OEM depressurization procedure.
clarifyingQuestions: Does the concern occur under hard acceleration or high load, at idle, or during cold or hot restarts?
Is there any fuel odor, smoke, rough start, or misfire, especially after a hot soak?
Has there been recent fuel system work (pump, injectors, lines) or a refueling just before the problem started?
What is the mileage and oil change history? High-pressure pump drive wear is mileage and lubrication related on some engines.
Are low-pressure fuel pump, pump control module, or pressure regulator control circuit codes also stored?

causes.title: High-pressure fuel pump or its integral control (metering) valve
causes.description: Internal wear or a sticking metering valve prevents the pump from building or controlling rail pressure. A valve stuck in the full-delivery position can drive pressure too high; internal leakage or reduced stroke causes pressure too low, especially at high demand. The pump outlet, lines, and rail operate at extremely high pressure and are extremely dangerous; never loosen a high-pressure fitting without first following the OEM depressurization procedure.

modifiers.reason: Rail pressure too low codes present
Pump shortfall appears at high demand

causes.title: Rail pressure sensor skewed, stuck, or intermittent
causes.description: The PCM controls the pump from the rail pressure sensor. A sensor that reads high makes the PCM under-deliver (and can set pressure-too-high codes); one that reads low makes it over-deliver. An erratic sensor sets range/performance codes.

modifiers.reason: Rail pressure sensor range/performance code present
Rail pressure sensor circuit code present
A sensor reading high can produce pressure-too-high codes

causes.title: Inadequate low-side supply to the high-pressure pump
causes.description: The high-pressure pump can only compress the fuel it receives. A weak in-tank pump, restricted filter, or low-side control fault starves the high-pressure pump and rail pressure falls, particularly under load.

modifiers.reason: Low fuel system pressure code present
Low-pressure pump circuit or control codes present
Low supply cannot cause pressure too high
Low fuel level or fuel starvation reported

causes.title: Leaking or stuck-open direct injector
causes.description: A direct injector that leaks or sticks open bleeds rail pressure into a cylinder, lowering rail pressure and causing hard hot starts, misfire, smoke, and fuel dilution of the oil.

modifiers.reason: A leaking injector lowers rather than raises rail pressure

causes.title: Worn high-pressure pump follower or drive cam lobe
causes.description: Where the high-pressure pump is driven by a camshaft lobe through a follower or tappet, wear reduces pump stroke so rail pressure falls at high demand; continued operation can destroy the cam lobe.

modifiers.reason: Reduced stroke shows at high demand
Reduced stroke cannot cause pressure too high

causes.title: Pump control valve or rail sensor wiring or connector fault
causes.description: Open, shorted, or high-resistance wiring or connectors in the pump control valve circuit or the rail pressure sensor circuit prevent correct pressure control or corrupt the pressure signal.

modifiers.reason: Fuel pressure regulator control circuit codes present
Rail pressure sensor circuit codes present

causes.title: PCM calibration requiring an update
causes.description: OEMs frequently revise high-pressure pump control strategy and pressure diagnostic thresholds; an outdated calibration can set pressure control codes on an otherwise healthy system.

modifiers.reason: Pressure control performance codes are common subjects of calibration updates

causes.title: Contaminated or incorrect fuel
causes.description: Water, debris, or the wrong fuel damages the high-pressure pump and injectors and can prevent pressure control.

modifiers.reason: Problem began after refueling or wrong fuel reported

tests.title: Graph rail pressure desired vs actual and pump control command
tests.purpose: Characterize how rail pressure fails (lags at load, low everywhere, above desired, or implausible) without opening the system.
procedure: Record all DTCs and freeze frame data, including rail pressure desired and actual if stored.
Graph rail pressure desired, rail pressure actual, the pump control (metering valve) command, and low-side pressure at idle.
Perform snap throttle and a loaded road test or dynamometer run that reproduces the freeze-frame conditions.
Note whether actual lags desired with the control command at its limit, stays low everywhere, rises above desired, or behaves implausibly (stuck, jumping, not reacting to start).
tools: Scan tool with rail pressure and pump control PIDs
tests.expected: Actual rail pressure closely follows desired in all conditions, and the pump control command stays within its normal range per OEM service information.
tests.specNote: Rail pressure ranges and control command limits per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Actual tracks desired in all conditions
outcomes.interpretation: The fault is not present now; consider an intermittent circuit fault or a calibration issue, and check bulletins.

outcomes.label: Actual falls behind desired as demand rises, with the control command at its limit
outcomes.interpretation: Delivery capacity is short. Confirm the low-side supply first, then evaluate the high-pressure pump and its drive.

outcomes.label: Actual below desired at idle and under load
outcomes.interpretation: Check for a leak path (injector or pump internal leakage) and a control circuit fault in addition to supply problems.

outcomes.label: Actual rises above desired with the control command at minimum
outcomes.interpretation: Either the pump is over-delivering (metering valve stuck or control circuit fault) or the sensor is reading high; verify the sensor before replacing the pump.

outcomes.label: Rail pressure reading implausible (stuck, jumping, or not reacting to start)
outcomes.interpretation: Test the rail pressure sensor circuit and its key-on plausibility.

tests.title: Verify low-side supply pressure to the high-pressure pump
tests.purpose: Rule out low-side starvation before condemning the high-pressure pump.
procedure: Using the low-side pressure PID, or a gauge connected only to the low-pressure supply test point per the OEM procedure, record supply pressure at key-on prime and idle.
Graph low-side desired vs actual during snap throttle and a loaded road test.
If using a gauge, relieve low-side pressure per the OEM procedure before connecting and after testing, keep a fire extinguisher nearby, and never connect to the high-pressure rail or lines.
Compare readings with the OEM specification and note any drop coinciding with rail pressure loss.
tools: Scan tool with low-side pressure PID
Low-pressure fuel gauge and adapters (if no PID)
tests.expected: Low-side supply pressure meets the OEM specification and tracks desired, including under load.
tests.specNote: Low-side supply pressure specification per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Low-side supply adequate in all conditions
outcomes.interpretation: The high-pressure pump is being fed properly; focus on the high-pressure side, sensor, and control.

outcomes.label: Low-side supply pressure below desired or specification
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the low-pressure system (pump, filter, regulator, pump control) and retest rail pressure after repair.

outcomes.label: No low-side PID and no accessible low-side test point
outcomes.interpretation: Use the OEM-approved adapter or continue with other tests.

tests.title: Visual inspection of the high-pressure pump, rail, lines, and connectors (engine off)
tests.purpose: Identify external leaks, fuel odor, damaged connectors, or wiring faults at the pump control valve and rail sensor.
procedure: With the engine off and cool, inspect the high-pressure pump, lines, rail, and injector areas for wetness, fuel odor, or staining. Do not start the engine if a high-pressure leak is suspected.
Inspect the pump control valve and rail pressure sensor connectors for corrosion, fuel intrusion, broken locks, or pushed-back terminals.
Follow the harness for chafing, heat damage, or non-OEM repairs.
Check engine oil for a strong fuel odor or rising level, which can indicate injector leakage or pump seal leakage into the crankcase on some designs.
tests.expected: No fuel leaks or odor, connectors and wiring intact, and engine oil without fuel dilution.

outcomes.label: No leaks, damage, or oil dilution found
outcomes.interpretation: Continue with electrical and pressure testing.

outcomes.label: Damaged or corroded connector or wiring at the pump control valve or rail sensor
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the wiring or connector and retest before replacing components.

outcomes.label: External fuel leak, fuel odor at the high-pressure components, or fuel-diluted oil
outcomes.interpretation: Do not run the engine with a high-pressure leak. Relieve pressure per the OEM procedure and repair; replace single-use lines, seals, and fasteners where the OEM requires. Fuel-diluted oil points toward injector or pump seal leakage.

tests.title: Check TSBs, recalls, and PCM calibration level
tests.purpose: Pressure control codes on direct-injection engines are often addressed by calibration updates or revised parts.
procedure: Enter the VIN in the OEM service portal and list open recalls and bulletins for the stored DTCs and symptoms.
Read the current PCM calibration ID with the scan tool and compare it with the latest available calibration.
Review bulletin instructions for any required pre-checks before reprogramming or parts replacement.
Maintain stable battery voltage with a suitable power supply during any reprogramming.
tools: Battery maintainer or programming power supply
tests.expected: The PCM calibration is current and no bulletin applies, or the bulletin procedure is followed.

outcomes.label: A calibration update applies to these codes or symptoms
outcomes.interpretation: Perform the update per the bulletin, clear codes, and verify under the freeze-frame conditions before replacing parts.

outcomes.label: A bulletin or recall covers the pump, pump drive, sensor, or injectors
outcomes.interpretation: Follow the bulletin's diagnostic steps to confirm the condition before replacing the listed part.

outcomes.label: Calibration current and no applicable bulletin
outcomes.interpretation: Software is unlikely; continue with pressure and circuit testing.

tests.title: Rail pressure sensor circuit and key-on plausibility check
tests.purpose: Confirm the rail pressure sensor reads correctly before trusting any pressure-based conclusion.
procedure: After a cold soak of the length described in service information, turn the key on without starting and read rail pressure before the pump primes, comparing it with the OEM-described value for that condition.
Back-probe the sensor and measure reference voltage, ground voltage drop, and signal with the key on; compare the signal with the scan tool value.
With the engine running, view the signal on a lab scope while snapping the throttle; look for dropouts, noise, or flat spots.
Wiggle the harness between the sensor and PCM while watching the signal.
tests.expected: Key-on reading matches the OEM-described soaked value; reference, ground, and signal are within specification, and the signal is smooth with no dropouts.
tests.specNote: Soak time, key-on expected value, reference voltage, and signal range per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Key-on value plausible and circuits good
outcomes.interpretation: The sensor can be trusted; pressure faults are real and originate elsewhere.

outcomes.label: Sensor reports a clear offset at key-on after a soak
outcomes.interpretation: A skewed sensor is likely. Confirm the circuit is good; some sensors are only serviced with the rail, so follow the OEM procedure.

outcomes.label: Reference, ground, or signal circuit fault found
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the circuit and retest; if the reference is pulled low, check other sensors that share it.

outcomes.label: Signal noisy or drops out with good reference and ground
outcomes.interpretation: An internally failing sensor or intermittent signal wire; repeat the wiggle test before replacing the sensor.

tests.title: High-pressure pump control valve circuit and command waveform
tests.purpose: Separate a pump control valve or winding fault from harness or connector faults.
procedure: With the key off, inspect the pump control valve connector, then measure valve winding resistance at the valve and compare with the OEM specification.
Check the control circuits from the PCM to the valve for opens, shorts to ground or voltage, and excessive resistance per the wiring diagram.
With the engine running, capture the valve command on a lab scope (voltage and, if available, current) and compare its shape with OEM or known-good reference data.
Review any regulator control circuit codes and their freeze-frame conditions.
tests.expected: Valve winding resistance within the OEM specification, control circuits intact, and a command waveform with normal shape and current.
tests.specNote: Valve resistance and command characteristics per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Valve winding, circuits, and command waveform normal
outcomes.interpretation: The control side is good; a pressure shortfall is mechanical (pump, drive, supply, or leakage) or the sensor is misreporting.

outcomes.label: Open, short, or high resistance in the harness or connector
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the circuit and retest before replacing the pump.

outcomes.label: Valve winding resistance or current signature out of specification
outcomes.interpretation: The control valve is faulty; on most designs it is serviced only with the high-pressure pump.

tests.title: Rail pressure hold and decay after shutdown
tests.purpose: Detect a leak path (injector, pump outlet or relief valve) that bleeds rail pressure after the engine stops.
procedure: Warm the engine to operating temperature and confirm rail pressure is stable at idle.
Shut the engine off and immediately return the key to on (engine off) with the scan tool recording rail pressure.
Record the decay over the time interval given in service information and compare with the expected behavior or a known-good vehicle.
If decay is rapid, look for cylinder-specific evidence (misfire counters on restart, fuel-washed plug, or OEM injector leak test) before replacing parts.
tools: Scan tool with rail pressure PID and recording
tests.expected: Rail pressure decays gradually as described by the OEM or matches a known-good vehicle.
tests.specNote: Expected pressure hold behavior per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Pressure decays normally
outcomes.interpretation: No significant leak path; an injector or pump leak is less likely.

outcomes.label: Pressure drops rapidly after shutdown
outcomes.interpretation: A leaking injector or pump outlet or relief valve is likely. Identify the cylinder (misfire on hot restart, fuel-wet plug, OEM leak test) before replacing injectors.

outcomes.label: Rail pressure PID not readable with the engine off
outcomes.interpretation: Use OEM injector leakage tests or misfire data on hot restart instead.

tests.title: Fuel quality sample
tests.purpose: Check for water, debris, or incorrect fuel that can damage the high-pressure pump and injectors.
procedure: Relieve low-side pressure per the OEM procedure; observe fire precautions.
Draw a sample from the low-pressure side or tank into a clear, approved container.
Allow it to settle and check for water separation, debris, cloudiness, or the odor or color of the wrong fuel.
If contamination is found, plan the OEM-directed cleaning and component inspection before running the engine further.
tests.expected: Clean, clear fuel of the correct type with no water or debris.

outcomes.label: Fuel sample clean
outcomes.interpretation: Contamination is unlikely.

outcomes.label: Water, debris, or wrong fuel found
outcomes.interpretation: Remove the contaminated fuel and inspect the pump, filter, and injectors per the OEM procedure; contamination may have damaged high-pressure components.

tests.title: Remove the high-pressure pump and inspect the follower and drive lobe
tests.purpose: Confirm or rule out follower or cam lobe wear before replacing the high-pressure pump.
procedure: Allow the engine to cool. Relieve high-pressure and low-pressure fuel pressure strictly per the OEM procedure; the high-pressure side can remain dangerously pressurized after shutdown.
Disconnect the battery if required by the OEM procedure, then remove the high-pressure lines and pump in the OEM sequence, catching fuel in an approved container.
Inspect the follower or tappet and the drive lobe for wear, scoring, flat spots, or missing coating, and compare with OEM wear criteria.
Reinstall with new single-use lines, seals, and fasteners where the OEM requires, tightened per the OEM specification.
Prime the system, check for leaks visually from a safe distance before and during the first start, and never touch a suspected high-pressure leak.
tests.expected: Follower and drive lobe within OEM wear criteria.
tests.specNote: Removal sequence, wear limits, and fastener torque per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Follower and drive lobe within limits
outcomes.interpretation: The pump drive is healthy; with the supply, sensor, and control circuit verified, the pump itself is the likely cause.

outcomes.label: Follower or drive lobe worn or damaged
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the worn follower (and camshaft if the lobe is damaged) per the OEM procedure, and inspect the pump for resulting damage.

verification: Record freeze frame data and clear DTCs.
Confirm rail pressure actual tracks desired, and low-side supply tracks desired, at idle, snap throttle, and full-load acceleration.
Inspect any disturbed high-pressure connection visually from a safe position with the engine running; never touch a suspected high-pressure leak.
Road test under the freeze-frame conditions and confirm the fuel pressure monitors complete with no DTC returning.

playbooks.title: Fuel injector circuit faults
playbooks.summary: Injector circuit codes mean the PCM detected an electrical fault in an injector control circuit, not a fuel delivery problem. Use the code pattern to separate a single injector or its wiring from a shared supply feed or PCM driver problem, then test supply voltage, pulse, coil resistance, and harness integrity before replacing an injector or PCM. On direct-injection engines, follow the OEM procedure because injector drive circuits operate at elevated voltage.
clarifyingQuestions: Which injector codes are set: one cylinder, several, or all? Are misfire codes also present?
Is the engine port injected or direct injected?
Has there been recent engine work (intake manifold, valve cover, injector replacement) that disturbed injector connectors or harnesses?
Is the fault intermittent, for example after rain, washing, or driving over bumps?
Was an injector or the PCM previously replaced for the same code?

causes.title: Injector with open or shorted coil
causes.description: An injector whose solenoid winding is open or shorted draws no current or excessive current, which the PCM driver detects as a circuit fault; the cylinder usually misfires.

modifiers.reason: Winding and seal failures increase with age

causes.title: Open, shorted, or chafed injector control or supply wiring
causes.description: Damaged wiring between the PCM and the injector (control side) or in the injector supply feed opens or shorts the circuit; harness rub points, heat damage, and rodent damage are common.

causes.title: Corroded, loose, or damaged injector connector
causes.description: A connector with corrosion, spread terminals, or a broken lock creates an intermittent open or high resistance at the injector.

modifiers.reason: Connector may not be fully seated after service

causes.title: Injector supply feed fault (fuse, relay, or shared splice)
causes.description: Injectors on many engines share a switched supply feed through a fuse, relay, or splice; a failure in that feed affects several or all injectors at once and can cause a no-start.

modifiers.reason: General injector circuit code suggests a shared fault

causes.title: PCM power or ground circuit fault
causes.description: Poor PCM power or ground connections disturb driver operation and diagnostics, typically setting several circuit codes at once.

modifiers.reason: PCM output or internal circuit codes present

causes.title: PCM injector driver failure
causes.description: A failed driver transistor inside the PCM cannot switch the injector. A shorted injector or wiring fault can damage the driver, so the root cause must be found before a PCM is replaced.

modifiers.reason: PCM output or internal circuit codes present
Code persists after an injector was replaced

tests.title: Review the injector code pattern and freeze frame
tests.purpose: The number and grouping of injector codes points to a single injector or circuit versus a shared feed, PCM power, or driver problem.
procedure: Record all DTCs from all modules, with freeze frame and DTC status (current, pending, history).
List which cylinders have injector circuit codes and whether P0200 or misfire codes are also set.
Using the wiring diagram, note which injectors share a supply feed, splice, or PCM driver group.
Note engine conditions when the code set (cranking, idle, temperature, load).
tests.expected: Documented code pattern mapped against the injector supply and driver layout.

outcomes.label: Code on one cylinder only
outcomes.interpretation: Focus on that injector, its connector, and its control wire.

outcomes.label: Codes on several injectors that share a feed, splice, or driver group
outcomes.interpretation: Look for the common element: the shared feed, splice, harness section, or driver group.

outcomes.label: All injectors affected or general code P0200
outcomes.interpretation: Check the injector supply fuse or relay and the PCM power and ground circuits first.

tests.title: Inspect injector connectors and harness routing
tests.purpose: Find loose, corroded, or damaged connectors and chafed or heat-damaged wiring before electrical testing.
procedure: With the key off, inspect the affected injector connector for a broken lock, corrosion, fuel or oil intrusion, and spread or pushed-back terminals.
Check terminal fit with the correct terminal test probe rather than a meter lead.
Trace the harness along the intake manifold, valve cover, and brackets for chafing, heat damage, rodent damage, or previous repairs.
Inspect the PCM connectors for corrosion or poor seating.
tests.expected: Connectors fully seated and locked, terminals clean with proper tension, and harness intact.

outcomes.label: Connectors and harness in good condition
outcomes.interpretation: Continue with electrical testing.

outcomes.label: Connector corroded, loose, unlocked, or with poor terminal tension
outcomes.interpretation: Repair or replace the connector or terminals with OEM-approved parts, then retest.

outcomes.label: Chafed, melted, or rodent-damaged wiring found
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the harness per the OEM wiring repair procedure; check for a damaged PCM driver if the circuit was shorted.

tests.title: Check injector supply voltage and control pulse at the connector
tests.purpose: Determine whether the injector connector receives supply voltage and a control pulse from the PCM.
procedure: Port injection: with the injector unplugged and the key on, verify supply voltage at the feed terminal using a DVOM or a test light.
Port injection: connect an injector test light (noid light) or lab scope to the connector and crank the engine to check for a control pulse.
Direct injection: do not use a noid light or jumper the circuits; drive circuits use elevated voltage, so check the pulse with a lab scope only as the OEM procedure directs.
Compare with an adjacent good cylinder.
tests.expected: Supply voltage present per OEM specification and a regular control pulse while cranking, matching a good cylinder.
tests.specNote: Supply voltage and pulse characteristics per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Supply voltage and control pulse present
outcomes.interpretation: Supply and control reach the connector; test the injector coil and the connector terminals.

outcomes.label: No supply voltage at the injector connector
outcomes.interpretation: Check the injector fuse or relay and trace the supply circuit. If the fuse is blown, find the short before replacing it.

outcomes.label: Supply present but no control pulse
outcomes.interpretation: Check the control wire between the PCM and the injector, then PCM power and ground, before condemning the PCM driver.

tests.title: Measure injector coil resistance
tests.purpose: Identify an injector with an open or shorted winding.
procedure: With the key off and the injector unplugged, measure resistance across the injector terminals.
Compare with the OEM specification at the current engine temperature and with the other injectors.
Check each terminal to the injector body for a short to ground where applicable.
For intermittent faults, repeat with the engine at operating temperature.
tests.expected: Resistance within the OEM specification and consistent with the other injectors; no short to the body.
tests.specNote: Injector resistance specification per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Resistance within specification
outcomes.interpretation: The winding is likely good; test the harness and driver.

outcomes.label: Open or resistance above specification
outcomes.interpretation: The injector winding is open or degraded; verify the injector-side terminals are clean before replacement.

outcomes.label: Resistance below specification or shorted to the body
outcomes.interpretation: The injector is shorted. A shorted injector can damage the PCM driver, so verify driver operation after replacement.

tests.title: Injector supply and control circuit integrity and wiggle test
tests.purpose: Locate opens, shorts, or high resistance between the PCM, supply feed, and injector.
procedure: Disconnect the battery if required by the OEM procedure before disconnecting the PCM connector.
Check continuity of the control circuit from the PCM terminal to the injector connector, and of the supply circuit from the fuse or relay to the injector.
Check each circuit for short to ground, short to voltage, and short to adjacent circuits.
Reconnect and perform a voltage drop test on the supply circuit while the injector operates, flexing the harness at rub points.
tools: Break-out box or terminal test leads
tests.expected: Circuits continuous with low resistance, no shorts, and no change during the wiggle test.

outcomes.label: Supply and control circuits intact
outcomes.interpretation: Wiring is good; focus on the injector, the PCM driver, or PCM power and ground.

outcomes.label: Open or high resistance in the supply or control circuit
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the open or high-resistance section, including connector terminals, then retest.

outcomes.label: Short to ground, to voltage, or between circuits
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the short and check the PCM driver and the supply fuse afterward.

tests.title: Injector current waveform comparison
tests.purpose: Compare the suspect injector's current ramp with the other injectors to separate an injector fault from a circuit or driver fault.
procedure: Clamp a low-amp current probe around the injector supply wire (or the shared supply feed to view all injectors in sequence).
Capture the current waveforms at idle and while cranking if the engine does not run.
Compare the suspect injector's current rise, peak, and pintle signature with the other injectors or OEM reference data.
Note any injector with no current, abnormally fast rise, or high peak current.
tests.expected: All injectors show similar current waveforms consistent with OEM or known-good reference data.

outcomes.label: Suspect injector's current waveform matches the others
outcomes.interpretation: The injector and circuit are operating now; the fault is likely intermittent. Perform a wiggle test while monitoring.

outcomes.label: Abnormal current ramp or peak on the suspect injector
outcomes.interpretation: A shorted or sticking injector is likely; confirm the connector and terminals are sound.

outcomes.label: No current flow on the suspect injector(s)
outcomes.interpretation: The circuit is open or not being driven; check supply, control wire, and PCM driver.

tests.title: PCM power and ground voltage drop test
tests.purpose: Verify the PCM has good power and ground before condemning its injector driver.
procedure: Identify all PCM power, ignition, and ground terminals from the wiring diagram.
With the key on (and engine running if possible), measure voltage drop from battery positive to each PCM power terminal.
Measure voltage drop from each PCM ground terminal to battery negative with the circuits loaded.
Inspect PCM ground points on the engine and body for corrosion and tightness.
tests.expected: Voltage drops on PCM power and ground circuits are small (general guideline: a few tenths of a volt or less — verify against OEM specification).

outcomes.label: PCM power and ground circuits good
outcomes.interpretation: With good power and ground, a missing pulse with an intact control wire points to the PCM driver; follow the OEM procedure before replacing and programming a PCM.

outcomes.label: Excessive voltage drop on a PCM power or ground circuit
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the power or ground fault and retest; the injector codes may be a symptom of it.

tests.title: Check TSBs and recalls for injector harness, injectors, or PCM
tests.purpose: Harness rub points, connector issues, and PCM driver concerns are sometimes documented in bulletins.
procedure: Search the OEM service portal by VIN, DTC, and symptom.
Review harness routing and connector bulletins for the affected engine.
Note any required revised parts or repair procedures.
tools: OEM service portal or professional information system
tests.expected: No applicable bulletin, or the bulletin's diagnostic steps are followed.

outcomes.label: Bulletin covers injector harness, connector, or PCM
outcomes.interpretation: Inspect the documented location and follow the bulletin repair.

outcomes.label: Bulletin covers the injectors
outcomes.interpretation: Confirm the injector fault by testing before replacement.

outcomes.label: No applicable bulletin
outcomes.interpretation: Continue with electrical testing.

verification: Clear DTCs and confirm no injector circuit code resets during key-on, cranking, and idle.
Monitor misfire counters and fuel trims on the affected bank to confirm the injector is contributing normally.
Wiggle the repaired harness section with the engine running and confirm no misfire or code.
Road test under the freeze-frame conditions and confirm no DTC returns.

playbooks.title: EVAP system leak detected
playbooks.summary: EVAP leak codes mean the PCM's leak test found that the sealed fuel vapor system could not hold vacuum or pressure. Check the cap and filler neck first, confirm the leak with the OEM EVAP system test, then locate it with an EVAP-rated smoke test before replacing parts. Vent and purge valves that do not seal and a skewed tank pressure sensor mimic leaks and must be ruled out.
clarifyingQuestions: Did the code set shortly after refueling, and was the cap tightened correctly or recently replaced with a non-OEM cap?
Is there a fuel vapor odor, and where is it strongest?
Has the vehicle had recent fuel pump, fuel tank, or rear body work?
Is the tank hard to fill, or does the nozzle shut off early? Does the owner habitually top off after the nozzle clicks off?
Does the vehicle have a capless filler, and is it driven on dusty or gravel roads?

causes.title: Fuel cap loose, damaged, or incorrect (or capless filler seal)
causes.description: A cap that is loose, cross-threaded, has a damaged seal, or is not the correct type lets the system vent to atmosphere, and the leak test fails.

modifiers.reason: Leak detected (fuel cap loose/off) code present
Large leaks are often an open or loose cap
Complaint relates to refueling or the cap

causes.title: Cracked, disconnected, or damaged EVAP hose or line
causes.description: Aged rubber hoses crack, quick-connect seals leak, and lines are damaged by road debris, rodents, or previous repairs.

modifiers.reason: Small leaks are often cracked hoses or seals

causes.title: Canister vent valve not sealing
causes.description: A vent valve that sticks open or leaks (often from dirt, debris, or insect nests in the vent path) cannot seal the system for the leak test.

modifiers.reason: Large leak consistent with a vent stuck open
Vent control circuit or performance code present
Debris entry through the vent path
Vent valves wear and collect debris

causes.title: Purge valve not opening or leaking
causes.description: On engine-vacuum leak tests, a purge valve that does not open prevents vacuum from being drawn and reads as a large leak; one that leaks through lets the test vacuum or pressure escape.

modifiers.reason: No vacuum developed can be a purge valve that does not open
Purge flow or purge circuit code present

causes.title: Cracked or saturated charcoal canister
causes.description: A cracked canister body or damaged ports leaks; liquid fuel from topping off saturates the charcoal and can carry debris into the vent valve.

modifiers.match: top off|topping off|overfill|hard to fill|clicks off|shuts off
modifiers.reason: Overfilling or refueling problems damage canisters
Canister and port damage increase with age

causes.title: Corroded or damaged filler neck or filler vent line
causes.description: Rust at the cap sealing surface, a perforated filler pipe, or a cracked filler vent line lets vapor escape even with a good cap.

modifiers.reason: Cap-area or large leak code present

causes.title: Fuel tank pressure sensor skewed or erratic
causes.description: The leak test judges the system with the tank pressure sensor; an offset or erratic sensor can fail a sealed system.

causes.title: Leak detection pump or leak check module fault
causes.description: Systems that test for leaks with a dedicated pump or leak check module (often combined with the vent valve) report false leaks when the pump, its switch, or its reference check fails.

causes.title: Leaking fuel pump module seal or tank-top connection
causes.description: The pump module lock ring seal, sender seal, or tank-top line connections leak, particularly after pump replacement or tank removal.

modifiers.reason: Recent tank or pump module service

causes.title: EVAP monitor calibration issue
causes.description: Some leak monitors have been recalibrated by OEMs to correct false small-leak detections; an outdated calibration can set codes on a sealed system.

modifiers.reason: Very small leak detections are a common subject of recalibration

tests.title: Inspect and test the fuel cap and filler neck sealing surface
tests.purpose: Quickly confirm or rule out the most common cause of leak codes.
procedure: Confirm the cap is the correct part for the vehicle and inspect the seal for cracks, swelling, or debris; on capless fillers, inspect the flapper seal and door.
Test the cap on an EVAP cap tester with the correct adapter per the tester's instructions.
Inspect the filler neck sealing surface for rust, dents, or burrs, and the filler pipe and its vent line for damage.
Reinstall the cap until it clicks (or verify the capless seal closes fully).
tests.expected: Cap is the correct type and passes the cap tester; the filler neck sealing surface is smooth and undamaged.

outcomes.label: Cap passes and the filler neck is in good condition
outcomes.interpretation: The cap is unlikely to be the cause; continue with the system test and smoke test.

outcomes.label: Cap fails the tester, is damaged, or is the wrong type
outcomes.interpretation: Replace with the correct OEM-specification cap, then confirm with the OEM EVAP test or a smoke test before releasing.

outcomes.label: Filler neck sealing surface or filler pipe damaged or corroded
outcomes.interpretation: Confirm the leak location with smoke, then repair or replace the filler pipe.

tests.title: Run the OEM EVAP system leak test with the scan tool
tests.purpose: Confirm whether a leak is currently present and whether the system components respond, before searching for the leak.
procedure: Check the enable conditions for the OEM service test (fuel level range, temperatures, engine state) in service information.
Run the scan tool EVAP service or leak test and record the result and any component faults it reports.
If the vehicle has a leak detection pump or leak check module, run its self-test and reference check as directed.
Review Mode $06 EVAP test results for how far the result is from the threshold.
tools: Scan tool with EVAP service test and Mode $06
tests.expected: The EVAP test passes and component checks report no faults.
tests.specNote: Test enable conditions and pass criteria per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: System test passes
outcomes.interpretation: No leak now. Consider a cap that was later tightened, an intermittent leak, or a calibration issue; check bulletins and review freeze-frame conditions.

outcomes.label: Test confirms a leak
outcomes.interpretation: A leak is present; locate it with a smoke test.

outcomes.label: Test aborts or reports a valve, pump, or sensor fault
outcomes.interpretation: Test the reported component (valve operation, pump self-test, or pressure sensor) before searching for leaks.

outcomes.label: Service test not supported or enable conditions cannot be met
outcomes.interpretation: Proceed directly to the smoke test.

tests.title: EVAP-rated smoke test with the vent sealed
tests.purpose: Locate the leak by introducing low-pressure smoke into the sealed EVAP system.
procedure: Use an EVAP-rated smoke machine supplied as the OEM directs (many require an inert gas such as nitrogen); never pressurize the system with shop air or above the machine's EVAP test setting.
Work in a ventilated area away from ignition sources, engine off, and have a fire extinguisher at hand.
Seal the system: command the vent valve closed with the scan tool (or cap the vent outlet per the OEM procedure) and confirm the purge valve is closed.
Connect to the EVAP service port (or the OEM-specified connection point) and introduce smoke; use the machine's flow indicator to judge whether a leak exists.

Inspect the cap and filler neck, engine bay lines, purge valve, underbody lines, canister, vent valve and vent outlet, and tank top with a bright light; check the intake for smoke passing through the purge valve.
Remove the equipment, restore the vent valve to normal, and clear any codes set by the test.
tools: EVAP-rated smoke machine with flow indicator
Scan tool with EVAP valve controls
tests.expected: With the system sealed, the flow indicator shows no flow and no smoke escapes anywhere.

outcomes.label: No smoke escapes and no flow indicated
outcomes.interpretation: The system seals. Suspect a purge valve that does not open (no vacuum during the monitor), a pressure sensor or pump fault, or an intermittent leak.

outcomes.label: Smoke at the cap, capless seal, or filler neck
outcomes.interpretation: Determine whether the cap seal or the neck surface is leaking; repeat with a known-good cap.

outcomes.label: Smoke at a hose, line, or connection
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the leaking hose, line, or quick-connect seal and re-smoke.

outcomes.label: Smoke at the canister, vent valve, or vent outlet
outcomes.interpretation: Smoke from the vent outlet with the vent commanded closed indicates a vent valve that is not sealing; smoke from the canister body indicates a cracked canister.

outcomes.label: Smoke at the tank top, pump module seal, or sensor seal
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the module seal or tank-top connection per the OEM procedure, observing fuel handling precautions.

outcomes.label: Smoke passes into the intake through the closed purge valve
outcomes.interpretation: The purge valve leaks when closed; confirm with a vacuum hold test on the valve before replacement.

outcomes.label: Could not connect or seal the system for testing
outcomes.interpretation: Use the OEM-specified connection point or adapters, or run the OEM service test.

tests.title: Visual inspection of EVAP lines, canister, vent, and filler pipe
tests.purpose: Find obvious damage, disconnections, or debris before or alongside smoke testing.
procedure: Safely raise and support the vehicle.
Trace the EVAP lines from the engine bay purge valve to the canister and tank for cracks, disconnections, rub-through, and rodent damage.
Inspect the canister, vent valve, vent hose, and vent filter for cracks, mud, insects, or blockage.
Inspect the filler pipe and its vent line for rust or damage, and the tank top for fuel odor or wetness.
tools: Lift or jack and jack stands
tests.expected: Lines connected and intact; canister, vent components, and filler pipe free of damage and debris.

outcomes.label: No visible damage or debris
outcomes.interpretation: Continue with the smoke test; many leaks are not visible.

outcomes.label: Cracked, disconnected, or damaged EVAP hose or line
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the line and confirm with a smoke test.

outcomes.label: Canister, vent path, filler pipe, or tank-top damage, debris, or wetness
outcomes.interpretation: Clean or repair the vent path, or repair the damaged component, and confirm with a smoke test.

tests.title: Command the vent valve closed and verify it seals
tests.purpose: Confirm the vent valve actually closes and holds when commanded.
procedure: Locate the vent valve and disconnect the hose between the canister and the valve if accessible, or test through the vent outlet per the OEM procedure.
Command the vent valve closed with the scan tool and listen or feel for it to actuate.
Apply vacuum with a hand pump (or low-pressure smoke) to the valve and verify it holds while commanded closed and releases when commanded open.
Inspect the valve inlet and vent filter for debris or charcoal granules.
tools: Scan tool with vent valve control
Hand vacuum pump or smoke machine
tests.expected: The valve actuates on command, holds vacuum when closed, and releases when open.

outcomes.label: Vent valve seals when commanded closed
outcomes.interpretation: The vent valve is not the leak path.

outcomes.label: Vent valve does not seal or does not actuate
outcomes.interpretation: Check for debris or charcoal from the canister holding the valve open; a saturated canister must be addressed or the new valve will fail too. Check the circuit if the valve does not actuate.

tests.title: Verify the purge valve opens when commanded and seals when off
tests.purpose: A purge valve that does not open reads as a large leak on vacuum-based tests; one that leaks lets test vacuum escape.
procedure: With the engine off, disconnect the canister-side purge hose and apply vacuum to the valve with a hand pump; it should hold (closed) per the OEM design.
With the engine idling, command purge on in steps with the scan tool and confirm vacuum at the canister-side port increases with command.
Command purge off and confirm vacuum at the port drops away.
Inspect the purge hose for collapse, kinks, or disconnection.
tests.expected: The valve holds vacuum when off and flows vacuum in proportion to the command.

outcomes.label: Opens with command and seals when off
outcomes.interpretation: The purge valve is operating correctly.

outcomes.label: No vacuum at the canister side when commanded on
outcomes.interpretation: Check the purge valve circuit and the vacuum supply hose; a valve that will not open prevents the leak test from drawing vacuum.

outcomes.label: Valve leaks vacuum when commanded off
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the purge valve and check the canister for liquid fuel or charcoal carried into the valve.

tests.title: Fuel tank pressure sensor plausibility check
tests.purpose: Verify the pressure sensor the leak test depends on reads correctly.
procedure: Remove the fuel cap so the tank is at atmospheric pressure and read the tank pressure PID; compare with the OEM-described reading at atmosphere.
Reinstall the cap, command the vent closed, and apply a small, controlled vacuum or pressure (purge command or smoke machine); confirm the PID changes smoothly and returns when released.
Check sensor reference voltage, ground, and signal at the connector per the wiring diagram.
Watch for dropouts while wiggling the harness.
tools: Hand vacuum pump or smoke machine
tests.expected: The PID reads the OEM-described value at atmosphere and responds smoothly to pressure changes; circuits within specification.
tests.specNote: Expected reading at atmosphere and circuit values per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Sensor reads correctly and responds
outcomes.interpretation: The sensor can be trusted.

outcomes.label: Offset at atmosphere, sluggish, stuck, or erratic
outcomes.interpretation: Check the sensor circuit; if the circuit is good, the sensor is faulty.

tests.title: Check TSBs, recalls, and monitor calibration updates
tests.purpose: EVAP components and monitor calibrations are frequent subjects of bulletins and emissions warranty coverage.
procedure: Search the OEM service portal by VIN, DTC, and symptom.
Compare the PCM calibration ID with the latest release.
Check extended emissions warranty coverage for EVAP components.
tests.expected: No applicable bulletin, or the bulletin procedure is followed.

outcomes.label: Bulletin covers an EVAP component
outcomes.interpretation: Follow the bulletin's diagnostic steps to confirm the component before replacing it.

outcomes.label: Monitor recalibration applies
outcomes.interpretation: Confirm the system seals with a smoke test, then reprogram per the bulletin.

outcomes.label: No applicable bulletin
outcomes.interpretation: Continue with standard diagnosis.

verification: Clear DTCs and run the OEM EVAP service test if available; confirm it passes.
Re-smoke the system after repairs and confirm no smoke escapes with the vent sealed.
Confirm the EVAP monitor completes and passes; enable conditions (fuel level, temperatures, cold soak) per the OEM may require an overnight soak and a specific drive cycle.
Confirm no fuel vapor odor remains around the vehicle or in the cabin.

playbooks.title: EVAP purge and vent control faults
playbooks.summary: Purge and vent codes are either electrical (solenoid circuit codes) or functional (incorrect, high, or low purge flow). For circuit codes, test the solenoid winding, feed, and control circuits before replacing a valve; for flow codes, command the valves with the scan tool and verify vacuum, flow, and sealing, including the vent path and canister. A purge valve stuck open commonly causes hard starting or rough running right after refueling, while a blocked vent causes slow fueling and tank vacuum.
clarifyingQuestions: Does the engine start hard or run rough right after refueling?
Is the tank hard to fill, or does the nozzle click off repeatedly?
When the fuel cap is removed, is there a strong rush of air into the tank?
Does the owner habitually top off the tank after the nozzle clicks off?
Are other EVAP codes (leak or tank pressure sensor codes) also stored?

causes.title: Purge valve stuck open, stuck closed, or with a failed winding
causes.description: A purge valve stuck open draws tank vapor and vacuum continuously (high flow, rich after refueling); one stuck closed or with an open winding gives no purge flow.

modifiers.reason: High purge flow code indicates flow when not commanded
Incorrect or low purge flow code present
Symptoms after refueling suggest purge stuck open

causes.title: Vent valve stuck, sluggish, or with a failed winding
causes.description: A vent valve stuck closed blocks fresh air to the canister (slow fueling, tank vacuum); stuck open, it prevents sealing; an open or shorted winding sets vent circuit codes.

modifiers.reason: Vent control circuit or performance code present

modifiers.match: hard to fill|clicks off|shuts off|won'?t fill|whoosh|rush of air|tank (collapse|deform)

modifiers.reason: Debris entry through the vent path

causes.title: Blocked vent hose or vent filter
causes.description: Mud, road debris, or insect nests block the vent hose or filter, so the canister cannot breathe; refueling is slow and tank vacuum builds during purge.

modifiers.match: hard to fill|clicks off|whoosh|rush of air|dust|mud|off.?road|insect|spider|wasp

causes.title: Saturated or restricted charcoal canister
causes.description: Liquid fuel from overfilling saturates the charcoal, restricts flow, and carries granules into the purge and vent valves.

modifiers.match: top off|topping off|overfill|hard to fill|clicks off

modifiers.reason: Low or incorrect purge flow code present

causes.title: Disconnected, collapsed, or cracked purge line
causes.description: A purge line that is off, collapsed, or cracked between the canister, purge valve, and intake prevents the monitor from seeing expected flow and may create a vacuum leak.

modifiers.reason: Incorrect or low purge flow code present

causes.title: Purge or vent solenoid feed or control wiring fault
causes.description: An open or shorted feed or control wire (or a blown shared fuse) disables the solenoid or leaves it energized. A control wire shorted to ground on a low-side-driven valve can hold the valve open.

causes.title: Corroded or loose purge or vent solenoid connector
causes.description: Underbody vent solenoid connectors are exposed to water and road salt; corrosion causes intermittent opens and circuit codes.

causes.title: Fuel tank pressure sensor skewed or erratic
causes.description: Many purge flow monitors judge flow by the change in tank pressure; a skewed or sluggish sensor sets incorrect, high, or low purge flow codes.

causes.title: PCM purge or vent driver failure
causes.description: A failed output driver cannot switch the solenoid. Shorted solenoids can damage drivers, so verify the solenoid before replacing a PCM.

causes.title: Purge flow monitor calibration issue
causes.description: Purge flow monitors are sometimes recalibrated to correct false detections.

tests.title: Command purge with the scan tool and watch the engine and tank response
tests.purpose: Check purge function non-invasively: commanded purge should change fuel trim, idle, and tank pressure; zero command should produce no flow.
procedure: Warm the engine to operating temperature and let it idle with accessories off.
With purge commanded off, record short-term fuel trim, RPM, and tank pressure; they should be stable.
Command purge up in steps and watch for short-term fuel trim to move (typically negative with fuel vapor present), idle to change, and tank pressure to move toward vacuum.
Command purge off again and confirm the response stops.
tools: Scan tool with purge control, fuel trim, and tank pressure PIDs
tests.expected: No response with purge commanded off; clear, proportional response when purge is commanded on.

outcomes.label: Engine and tank pressure respond to purge command and stop when off
outcomes.interpretation: Purge works; focus on the vent path, the tank pressure sensor, or calibration.

outcomes.label: No response when purge is commanded on
outcomes.interpretation: No purge flow: check the solenoid circuit, the valve itself, the purge lines, and the canister.

outcomes.label: Engine or tank pressure shows purge flow with purge commanded off
outcomes.interpretation: The purge valve is stuck or leaking open, or its control circuit keeps it energized; confirm with a vacuum test and a circuit check.

tests.title: Purge and vent solenoid winding, feed, and control circuit test
tests.purpose: Separate a failed solenoid winding from wiring, connector, fuse, or driver faults when circuit codes are present.
procedure: Inspect the solenoid connector for corrosion, broken locks, and terminal fit.
With the connector unplugged, measure solenoid winding resistance and compare with the OEM specification.
Key on: verify supply voltage at the feed terminal (check the fuse if missing).
