Connect a test light across the harness terminals and command the solenoid on and off with the scan tool; the light should follow the command.
If the command does not reach the connector, check the control wire for opens and shorts back to the PCM.
tests.expected: Winding resistance within the OEM specification, supply present, and control follows the scan tool command.
tests.specNote: Solenoid resistance and circuit layout per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Winding, supply, and control all good
outcomes.interpretation: Electrical side is good; test the valve mechanically (flow and sealing).

outcomes.label: Solenoid winding open, shorted, or out of specification
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the faulty solenoid valve; if it was shorted, confirm the PCM driver still switches correctly.

outcomes.label: Missing supply, blown fuse, or open or shorted control wire
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the wiring, connector, or cause of the blown fuse, then retest.

outcomes.label: Wiring good to the PCM but no output when commanded
outcomes.interpretation: Verify PCM power and ground, then follow the OEM procedure for PCM driver faults.

tests.title: Vacuum test the purge valve for sealing and opening
tests.purpose: Confirm whether the purge valve is stuck open, stuck closed, or working.
procedure: Disconnect the canister-side purge hose at the valve.
With the valve de-energized, apply vacuum with a hand pump; it should hold per the OEM design (most valves are normally closed).
Energize the valve by scan tool command (or a fused jumper per the OEM procedure) and confirm vacuum releases or flow passes.
Inspect the valve ports for charcoal granules or liquid fuel.
tests.expected: Holds vacuum when off and opens when energized.

outcomes.label: Seals when off and opens when energized
outcomes.interpretation: The purge valve works; if purge flow was absent, check lines, canister, and circuits.

outcomes.label: Leaks vacuum when off
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the purge valve; if charcoal is present, address the canister so the new valve is not contaminated.

outcomes.label: Does not open when energized
outcomes.interpretation: Confirm the valve receives power and command; if it does, replace the valve.

tests.title: Verify the vent valve opens freely and the vent path flows
tests.purpose: Detect a vent valve stuck closed or open, and a blocked vent hose, filter, or canister.
procedure: Safely raise and support the vehicle and locate the vent valve, vent hose, and filter.
With the valve commanded open (normally open on most designs), apply light vacuum or air flow through the vent path and confirm free flow per the OEM procedure.
Command the valve closed and confirm it seals.
Disconnect the vent hose and inspect the hose, filter, and valve inlet for mud, insects, or charcoal granules.
Remove the fuel cap after a drive and note any strong rush of air into the tank.
tools: Hand vacuum pump or smoke machine
tests.expected: Free flow when open, sealing when closed, clean vent path, and no strong tank vacuum when the cap is removed.

outcomes.label: Vent flows when open and seals when closed
outcomes.interpretation: The vent path is good.

outcomes.label: Restricted or no flow with the valve open, or strong tank vacuum
outcomes.interpretation: Find the restriction: vent filter or hose debris, a valve stuck closed, or a saturated canister.

outcomes.label: Valve does not seal when commanded closed
outcomes.interpretation: Check for debris holding the valve open, then replace the valve if it still leaks.

tests.title: Inspect purge lines, canister, and vent components
tests.purpose: Find disconnected or collapsed purge lines, saturated canisters, and blocked vents.
procedure: Trace the purge line from the intake to the purge valve and on to the canister; check for disconnection, collapse, kinks, and cracks.
Safely raise and support the vehicle and inspect the canister for cracks, liquid fuel, or fuel odor.
Check the purge valve inlet and vent valve for charcoal granules.
Inspect the vent hose and filter for mud, debris, or insect nests.
tests.expected: Lines intact and connected, canister dry and undamaged, vent path clean.

outcomes.label: No visible faults
outcomes.interpretation: Continue with functional and electrical tests.

outcomes.label: Purge line disconnected, collapsed, kinked, or cracked
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the line and retest purge function.

outcomes.label: Saturated canister, charcoal in valves, or blocked vent hose or filter
outcomes.interpretation: Clear or repair the vent path; replace a saturated canister along with any contaminated valves, and advise the owner not to top off.

tests.title: Fuel tank pressure sensor plausibility check
tests.purpose: Verify the tank pressure sensor that the purge flow monitor relies on.
procedure: Remove the fuel cap and read the tank pressure PID; compare with the OEM-described value at atmospheric pressure.
Reinstall the cap, command the vent closed, and command purge briefly at idle; the reading should move smoothly toward vacuum and recover when purge stops.
Check reference voltage, ground, and signal at the sensor connector.
Wiggle the harness while watching the PID for dropouts.
tests.expected: Correct reading at atmosphere and a smooth response to purge; circuits within the OEM specification.
tests.specNote: Expected sensor readings and circuit values per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Reading and response plausible
outcomes.interpretation: The sensor is working.

outcomes.label: Offset, sluggish, stuck, or erratic reading
outcomes.interpretation: Check the sensor circuit; if the circuit is good, the sensor is faulty.

tests.title: Check TSBs, recalls, and calibration updates for purge and vent systems
tests.purpose: Vent relocation kits, revised valves, and monitor recalibrations are common EVAP bulletins.
procedure: Search the OEM service portal by VIN, DTC, and symptom.
Compare the PCM calibration ID with the latest release.
Check extended emissions warranty coverage for EVAP components.
tests.expected: No applicable bulletin, or the bulletin procedure is followed.

outcomes.label: Bulletin covers a purge, vent, or canister component
outcomes.interpretation: Confirm the condition described in the bulletin before replacing parts.

outcomes.label: Monitor recalibration applies
outcomes.interpretation: Verify components function correctly, then reprogram per the bulletin.

outcomes.label: No applicable bulletin
outcomes.interpretation: Continue with standard diagnosis.

verification: Clear DTCs and command purge and vent with the scan tool; confirm the engine, tank pressure, and valves respond correctly.
Refuel (or simulate the refuel condition) and confirm normal starting and idle afterward, with no premature nozzle shutoff.
Complete the OEM drive cycle for the EVAP purge and leak monitors and confirm they pass with no DTC returning.
Confirm no fuel vapor odor and no strong tank vacuum when the cap is removed.

playbooks.title: EGR flow, control, and sensor faults
playbooks.summary: EGR flow codes (insufficient or excessive flow) are usually mechanical, such as carbon-clogged passages or a sticking valve, while control and sensor circuit codes are electrical. Command the valve with the scan tool and watch actual position and idle response to separate a valve that does not move from passages that do not flow, then verify feedback sensors and circuits before replacing the valve. Many flow monitors infer flow from MAP or a differential pressure sensor, so confirm those readings are plausible.
clarifyingQuestions: Is the EGR valve electrically actuated or vacuum operated, and does the system use a separate differential pressure or position feedback sensor?
Is there pinging or spark knock under acceleration, or rough idle and stalling at stops?
Is the vehicle used mostly for short trips, or does it consume oil (both accelerate carbon buildup)?
Are MAP sensor, misfire, or fuel trim codes also stored?
Has the vehicle failed an emissions test for NOx?

causes.title: Carbon-clogged EGR passages, ports, or tube
causes.description: Carbon builds up in the EGR tube, intake ports, or distribution passages until the valve opens but little exhaust flows, setting insufficient flow codes and allowing combustion temperatures (and NOx and pinging) to rise.

modifiers.reason: Excessive flow is not caused by restriction
Pinging under load suggests insufficient EGR
Operating conditions that accelerate carbon buildup

causes.title: EGR valve sticking, stuck open, or with a failed actuator or integral position sensor
causes.description: Carbon can hold the valve partly open (excess flow, rough idle, stalling) or prevent it from opening; the electric motor, vacuum diaphragm, or integral position sensor can also fail.

modifiers.reason: Excessive flow code suggests a valve stuck open
Control range/performance code: valve not following command
Position sensor code; sensor is often integral to the valve
Idle complaints suggest a valve stuck open
Valve wear and carbon increase with mileage

causes.title: EGR vacuum control solenoid or vacuum hose fault (vacuum-operated valves)
causes.description: On vacuum-operated systems, a failed control solenoid or a cracked, disconnected, or misrouted vacuum hose prevents the valve from opening, or holds it open.

causes.title: EGR differential pressure feedback sensor or its sensing hoses
causes.description: Systems that measure flow with a differential pressure sensor misjudge flow when the sensor drifts or its sensing hoses crack, melt, or plug with carbon.

modifiers.reason: Flow code may reflect a misreading sensor

causes.title: EGR control or sensor wiring fault
causes.description: Heat-damaged, chafed, or open wiring to the EGR valve, solenoid, or sensor sets control and sensor circuit codes.

modifiers.reason: Control or sensor circuit code present

causes.title: Corroded or loose EGR valve or sensor connector
causes.description: Connector corrosion or heat damage near the exhaust causes intermittent opens and signal errors.

modifiers.reason: Control or sensor circuit code present

causes.title: Restricted (or leaking) EGR cooler
causes.description: On engines with an EGR cooler, soot restricts the cooler and reduces flow; an internal leak causes coolant loss and white exhaust smoke.

modifiers.reason: Symptoms of cooler leakage or a diesel application

causes.title: MAP sensor skewed or slow (flow monitors that use MAP)
causes.description: Some PCMs judge EGR flow from the change in manifold pressure when EGR is commanded; a skewed or sluggish MAP sensor causes a false flow result.

causes.title: EGR monitor calibration issue
causes.description: Some EGR flow monitors have been recalibrated by OEMs to correct false failures.

tests.title: Command the EGR valve at idle and compare desired vs actual and engine response
tests.purpose: Separate a valve that does not move from passages that do not flow, and detect a valve stuck open.
procedure: Warm the engine to operating temperature and record freeze frame and EGR PIDs (desired and actual position, feedback sensor).
At idle with EGR commanded closed, note idle quality; a rough idle that smooths when the valve is disconnected or blocked per the OEM procedure suggests the valve is stuck open.

Command the valve open in steps with the scan tool (on vacuum-operated valves without output control, open it with a hand vacuum pump); where a position PID exists, watch actual position follow desired.
As the valve opens, idle should roughen or RPM drop noticeably if exhaust gas is flowing; note the response.
Return the command to closed (or release the vacuum) and confirm idle recovers.
tools: Scan tool with EGR output control and position PIDs
tests.expected: Actual position follows desired, idle roughens noticeably when EGR is commanded open, and idle is smooth with EGR closed.

outcomes.label: Valve follows the command and idle responds to flow
outcomes.interpretation: The valve and passages flow; suspect the feedback sensor, the MAP sensor used by the monitor, an intermittent circuit, or calibration.

outcomes.label: Valve follows the command but idle does not change
outcomes.interpretation: The valve moves but little exhaust flows: the passages, tube, or cooler are restricted.

outcomes.label: Actual position does not follow desired
outcomes.interpretation: Test the control circuit and (on vacuum systems) the vacuum supply, then the valve itself.

outcomes.label: Idle rough with EGR commanded closed, improves when the valve is blocked
outcomes.interpretation: The valve is stuck or leaking open; inspect it for carbon holding it off its seat.

outcomes.label: Valve could not be operated (no output control and no vacuum access)
outcomes.interpretation: Operate the valve per the OEM procedure, or inspect the valve and passages directly.

tests.title: Inspect EGR hoses, sensor lines, connectors, and tube
tests.purpose: Find cracked or disconnected vacuum and sensing hoses and damaged wiring before deeper testing.
procedure: With the engine off and cool, inspect vacuum hoses to the EGR valve and control solenoid for cracks, disconnection, and misrouting per the underhood label.
Inspect differential pressure sensor hoses for cracks, melting, or carbon plugging.
Inspect EGR valve and sensor connectors and wiring for heat damage and corrosion.
Check the EGR tube and flanges for exhaust leaks or damage.
tools: Vacuum hose routing label or diagram
tests.expected: Hoses intact and correctly routed, connectors and wiring undamaged, tube secure.

outcomes.label: No visible faults
outcomes.interpretation: Continue with functional tests.

outcomes.label: Vacuum or sensing hose cracked, melted, plugged, or misrouted
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the hose with heat-resistant hose of the correct type, route it correctly, and retest.

outcomes.label: Damaged wiring or corroded connector
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the wiring or connector and retest before replacing the valve or sensor.

tests.title: EGR feedback (position or differential pressure) sensor test
tests.purpose: Confirm the sensor that reports EGR position or flow reads correctly and its circuit is sound.
procedure: Key on, engine off: compare the sensor reading with the OEM-described value for a closed valve or zero flow.
Measure reference voltage, ground voltage drop, and signal at the sensor connector.
Operate the valve (scan tool command or hand vacuum pump) and confirm the signal changes smoothly without dropouts on a graphing meter or lab scope.
For differential pressure sensors, confirm the sensing hoses are connected to the correct ports and are not plugged.
tests.expected: Closed or zero-flow reading per the OEM description; smooth signal change with valve movement; circuits within the OEM specification.
tests.specNote: Sensor reference, signal range, and closed-valve reading per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Sensor reading and circuits plausible
outcomes.interpretation: The feedback signal can be trusted.

outcomes.label: Offset at rest, flat spots, or erratic signal with good circuits
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the separate sensor, or the valve if the position sensor is integral, after confirming the circuit.

outcomes.label: Reference, ground, or signal circuit fault
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the circuit and retest; check other sensors sharing the reference if it is pulled low.

tests.title: EGR valve motor or control solenoid circuit test
tests.purpose: Separate a failed valve actuator or solenoid winding from wiring and connector faults.
procedure: Unplug the valve or solenoid and measure the actuator or solenoid winding resistance; compare with the OEM specification.
Key on: verify supply voltage (if used) and ground at the harness connector.
Command the valve with the scan tool and verify the control signal at the connector with a lab scope or test light.
Check the control circuit to the PCM for opens and shorts if the command is missing.
tests.expected: Winding resistance within the OEM specification, supply and ground present, and control signal follows the command.
tests.specNote: Actuator resistance and circuit layout per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Actuator winding and circuits good
outcomes.interpretation: Electrical control is good; check mechanical operation and flow.

outcomes.label: Actuator or solenoid winding open, shorted, or out of specification
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the faulty valve or solenoid; verify the PCM driver still operates if the winding was shorted.

outcomes.label: Open, short, or missing supply in the harness
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the circuit and retest.

tests.title: Vacuum-operated EGR: diaphragm hold and control vacuum supply test
tests.purpose: On vacuum-operated valves, separate a leaking diaphragm from a missing control vacuum supply.
procedure: With the engine off, apply vacuum to the EGR valve with a hand pump and confirm the diaphragm holds vacuum and the valve stem or position reading moves.
Release the vacuum and confirm the valve returns fully closed.
Start the engine, reconnect the control hose through a tee to a vacuum gauge, and command EGR with the scan tool (or create the OEM-specified operating condition).
Confirm control vacuum reaches the valve when commanded and drops away when the command ends; if it does not, check the vacuum source hose and the control solenoid.
tests.expected: The diaphragm holds vacuum, the valve returns closed, and control vacuum reaches the valve only when commanded.

outcomes.label: Diaphragm holds and control vacuum arrives when commanded
outcomes.interpretation: Vacuum control and the diaphragm are good; check valve movement under flow, the passages, and the feedback sensor.

outcomes.label: Valve will not hold vacuum
outcomes.interpretation: The valve diaphragm is ruptured; replace the valve.

outcomes.label: No control vacuum at the valve when commanded, or vacuum present when not commanded
outcomes.interpretation: Check the control solenoid, its circuit, and the vacuum source and routing.

outcomes.label: Electric EGR valve (not applicable)
outcomes.interpretation: Use the scan tool command test and control circuit test instead.

tests.title: Remove the EGR valve and inspect the valve and passages for carbon
tests.purpose: Directly confirm carbon restriction or a valve held open before replacing parts.
procedure: Allow the engine to cool fully; exhaust components stay hot long after shutdown.
Remove the EGR valve (and tube if applicable) per the OEM procedure.
Inspect the valve pintle and seat for carbon holding it open or preventing movement.
Inspect the EGR port, tube, and accessible passages for restriction; follow the OEM cleaning procedure if carbon is present.
Reinstall with new gaskets, tightened per the OEM specification, and recheck for exhaust leaks.
tools: Carbon cleaning tools and OEM-approved cleaner
tests.expected: Valve seats and moves freely; passages open with only light deposits.
tests.specNote: Removal procedure, cleaning method, and fastener torque per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Valve and passages clean and free
outcomes.interpretation: Carbon is not the problem; revisit sensor, control, and monitor inputs.

outcomes.label: Valve carboned, sticking, or not seating
outcomes.interpretation: Clean or replace the valve per the OEM procedure and check the passages as well.

outcomes.label: Passages, port, or tube restricted with carbon
outcomes.interpretation: Clean the passages per the OEM procedure; inspect the cooler on engines so equipped.

tests.title: Check MAP sensor plausibility for MAP-based EGR flow monitors
tests.purpose: Confirm the manifold pressure input the flow monitor relies on is accurate and responsive.
procedure: Key on, engine off: compare the MAP reading with the barometric pressure PID or a known local barometric reading.
At idle and during a snap throttle, confirm MAP changes quickly and returns smoothly.
Inspect the MAP sensor vacuum source (if hose-fed) for leaks or blockage.
Command EGR open at idle and confirm MAP rises as expected when exhaust flows.
tests.expected: MAP matches barometric pressure at key on, responds quickly to throttle changes, and rises when EGR opens.

outcomes.label: MAP plausible and responsive
outcomes.interpretation: The MAP input can be trusted.

outcomes.label: MAP offset from baro, sluggish, or not responding to EGR
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the MAP sensor and its vacuum source before addressing EGR components.

tests.title: Check TSBs, recalls, and calibration updates for the EGR system
tests.purpose: EGR carbon cleaning procedures, revised valves, and monitor recalibrations are common bulletin topics.
procedure: Search the OEM service portal by VIN, DTC, and symptom.
Compare the PCM calibration ID with the latest release.
Check emissions warranty coverage for EGR components.
tests.expected: No applicable bulletin, or the bulletin procedure is followed.

outcomes.label: Bulletin covers EGR components or a cleaning procedure
outcomes.interpretation: Follow the bulletin's confirmation steps before repair.

outcomes.label: EGR monitor recalibration applies
outcomes.interpretation: Confirm the system functions correctly, then reprogram per the bulletin.

outcomes.label: No applicable bulletin
outcomes.interpretation: Continue with standard diagnosis.

verification: Clear DTCs and command the EGR valve with the scan tool; confirm actual position follows desired and idle responds to flow.
Confirm idle is smooth with EGR commanded closed.
Drive under the conditions required by the EGR monitor (per OEM drive cycle) and confirm it completes and passes.
Confirm no pinging under load and no DTC returns.

playbooks.title: Electronic throttle control, throttle position, and pedal position faults
playbooks.summary: Throttle and pedal position codes and reduced-power modes are set when the PCM sees disagreement between redundant sensors or between commanded and actual throttle position. Graph the sensor pairs and commanded vs actual throttle, then separate a failed throttle body or pedal assembly from wiring, connectors, a shared sensor reference voltage fault, low system voltage, or carbon binding before replacing parts. Keep fingers out of the throttle bore whenever the key is on, because the electronic throttle can move without warning.
clarifyingQuestions: When reduced power or limp mode occurs, is it after a cold start, over bumps, in rain, or at random?
Has the battery been weak, jump-started, or recently replaced, or has the charging system been serviced?
Was the throttle body recently cleaned or replaced, and was the OEM relearn performed?
Does the accelerator pedal move smoothly and return fully, with no floor mat interference?
Are several sensor codes (for example MAP, rail pressure, or other sensors on a shared reference voltage circuit) set at the same time?

causes.title: Failed electronic throttle body (motor, gears, or integral position sensors)
causes.description: Worn position sensor tracks, a weak motor, or stripped gears make throttle sensor 1 and 2 disagree or actual position fail to follow the command, forcing reduced power.

modifiers.reason: Throttle position sensor A or B code present
Throttle sensor A/B correlation code present
Throttle actuator control range/performance code present
Throttle stuck open or closed code present
Sensor track and gear wear increase with age

causes.title: Carbon buildup or ice binding the throttle plate
causes.description: Carbon at the plate edge or ice in cold, humid conditions makes the plate stick or restricts idle airflow, so actual position lags the command and stuck-throttle or idle codes set.

causes.title: Accelerator pedal position sensor assembly fault
causes.description: The redundant pedal sensors wear or glitch so their signals disagree, and the PCM limits throttle opening.

modifiers.reason: Pedal sensor D/E correlation code present
Position sensor C code (often the pedal on many designs)
Sensor A/B correlation usually refers to the throttle body

causes.title: Throttle or pedal sensor or motor wiring fault
causes.description: Chafed, stretched, or open wires in the throttle or pedal circuits cause intermittent signal loss or motor control faults, often triggered by engine movement or bumps.

modifiers.reason: Sensor circuit or correlation code present

causes.title: Corroded or fretted throttle body or pedal connector
causes.description: Water intrusion or terminal fretting at the throttle body connector causes intermittent high resistance and sensor disagreement.

causes.title: Low or unstable system voltage
causes.description: A weak battery, charging fault, or voltage dips during cranking or high electrical load can cause throttle actuator faults and reduced-power events.

modifiers.reason: Actuator performance code can be voltage related

causes.title: Shared sensor reference voltage circuit pulled down or open
causes.description: Throttle and pedal sensors often share reference voltage circuits with other sensors; a short in any sensor or its wiring on that reference corrupts several signals at once.

causes.title: PCM power or ground circuit fault
causes.description: High resistance in PCM power or ground circuits distorts sensor references and throttle motor control.

causes.title: Throttle control calibration issue
causes.description: Some throttle control and reduced-power diagnostics have been revised by OEM calibration updates.

modifiers.reason: Actuator performance or stuck codes are common update subjects

tests.title: Graph throttle and pedal sensor pairs and commanded vs actual throttle
tests.purpose: Identify which sensor pair or control loop disagrees, without disassembly.
procedure: Record all DTCs and freeze frame data from the PCM (and any separate throttle control module).
Graph throttle position sensors 1 and 2, pedal position sensors 1 and 2, and commanded vs actual throttle position.
Key on, engine off (where the OEM strategy moves the throttle), slowly press and release the pedal through its full travel several times; keep hands clear of the throttle body.
Start the engine and repeat with snap and slow throttle inputs; observe commanded vs actual throttle.
Look for dropouts, spikes, flat spots, or a sensor pair that stops agreeing, and note whether several unrelated sensors glitch together.
tests.expected: Each sensor pair tracks smoothly with its expected relationship through the full sweep, and actual throttle follows commanded without lag.
tests.specNote: Sensor voltage relationships and allowable disagreement per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: All pairs track and actual follows commanded
outcomes.interpretation: The fault is not present now; wiggle-test the harness and check system voltage and bulletins.

outcomes.label: Throttle sensor 1 and 2 disagree or drop out
outcomes.interpretation: Test the throttle body sensor circuits and connector before replacing the throttle body.

outcomes.label: Pedal sensor 1 and 2 disagree or drop out
outcomes.interpretation: Test the pedal sensor circuits and connector before replacing the pedal assembly.

outcomes.label: Actual throttle does not follow commanded (lag, sticking, or overshoot)
outcomes.interpretation: Inspect the throttle plate for carbon or ice, check system voltage, and test the throttle motor circuit.

outcomes.label: Several sensors on the same reference glitch or read offset together
outcomes.interpretation: Check the shared reference voltage circuit and PCM power and ground; unplug sensors on that reference one at a time to find a shorted sensor.

outcomes.label: Fault could not be reproduced
outcomes.interpretation: Monitor the PIDs during a road test and wiggle test under the freeze-frame conditions.

tests.title: Inspect the throttle bore, plate, and connector (key off)
tests.purpose: Find carbon, ice, or obstruction at the throttle plate and connector damage.
procedure: Turn the key off and wait for the PCM to power down (or disconnect the battery if the OEM procedure requires); keep fingers out of the bore whenever the key is on.
Remove the intake duct and inspect the throttle plate edge and bore for carbon, oil residue, ice, or debris.
Do not force the throttle plate by hand unless the OEM procedure permits it; some throttle bodies are damaged by manual movement.
Inspect the throttle body connector and terminals for corrosion, water, fretting, or bent pins.
tests.expected: Throttle plate and bore reasonably clean and dry, and the connector clean and tight.

outcomes.label: Bore clean and connector good
outcomes.interpretation: No carbon or connector fault; continue with electrical tests.

outcomes.label: Heavy carbon, sludge, or ice at the throttle plate
outcomes.interpretation: Clean per the OEM procedure (some bores have coatings that must not be scraped or solvent-cleaned), then perform the relearn and retest.

outcomes.label: Connector corroded, wet, fretted, or with poor terminal fit
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the connector or terminals and retest before replacing the throttle body.

tests.title: Battery, charging, and PCM power and ground check
tests.purpose: Rule out low or unstable voltage and PCM supply faults that cause throttle control errors.
procedure: Test the battery state of charge and capacity with a suitable battery tester.
Measure charging voltage at idle and with electrical loads on, and watch for dips during cranking.
Perform voltage drop tests on PCM (and throttle control module, if separate) power and ground circuits under load.
Check the battery terminals and main grounds for corrosion or looseness.
tests.expected: Battery and charging voltages within OEM specification, and small voltage drops on PCM power and ground (general guideline: a few tenths of a volt or less — verify against OEM specification).

outcomes.label: Battery, charging, and PCM supply good
outcomes.interpretation: Voltage supply is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Battery weak, charging low, or voltage dips under load
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the battery or charging fault, clear codes, and retest before replacing throttle components.

outcomes.label: Excessive voltage drop on PCM power or ground
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the power or ground connection and retest.

tests.title: Throttle and pedal sensor reference, ground, and signal tests
tests.purpose: Separate failed sensors from wiring, connector, and shared reference faults.
procedure: Back-probe the throttle body and pedal connectors; measure each sensor's reference voltage and ground (voltage drop) with the key on.
If a reference is low, unplug sensors that share it one at a time; recovery identifies a shorted sensor or branch.
Watch each signal on a lab scope or graphing meter during slow sweeps for glitches or flat spots.
Check signal and ground wires between the sensors and the PCM for opens, shorts, and resistance.
tests.expected: References and grounds within the OEM specification, and signals smooth and glitch-free through the sweep.
tests.specNote: Reference voltage, signal ranges, and pin assignments per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: References, grounds, and signals all good
outcomes.interpretation: Sensors and circuits are good; look at mechanical throttle operation, voltage, or calibration.

outcomes.label: Reference voltage low or missing (recovers when a sensor is unplugged, or not)
outcomes.interpretation: Find what is loading the reference (a shorted sensor or chafed wire); if nothing is, check PCM power and ground before suspecting the PCM.

outcomes.label: Open, short, or high resistance in a signal or ground wire
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the wiring or terminals and retest.

outcomes.label: Good reference and ground, but a sensor signal glitches or flat-spots
outcomes.interpretation: The sensor assembly (throttle body or pedal) is faulty; replace the assembly that contains the glitching sensor and perform the OEM relearn.

tests.title: Throttle actuator motor circuit test
tests.purpose: Separate a failed or binding throttle motor from motor control wiring faults.
procedure: Keep hands clear of the throttle bore; the plate can move whenever the key is on.
With the key off, unplug the throttle body and measure motor winding resistance; compare with the OEM specification.
Check both motor control circuits to the PCM for opens, shorts to ground or voltage, and resistance.
Reconnect and, with a lab scope and current probe, observe the motor control signal and current during a throttle sweep; compare with known-good data.
tests.expected: Motor resistance within the OEM specification, control circuits intact, and motor current and duty consistent with known-good data.
tests.specNote: Motor resistance and control characteristics per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Motor and control circuits normal
outcomes.interpretation: Motor control is sound; look at throttle sensors, carbon, or voltage.

outcomes.label: Motor resistance out of specification or abnormal current (binding)
outcomes.interpretation: Inspect for carbon binding first; if the bore is clean, the throttle body motor or gear train is faulty.

outcomes.label: Open, short, or resistance in a motor control circuit
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the circuit and retest.

tests.title: Wiggle test throttle and pedal harnesses while monitoring PIDs
tests.purpose: Reproduce intermittent faults caused by wiring or connectors.
procedure: Graph throttle sensors 1 and 2, pedal sensors 1 and 2, and commanded vs actual throttle.
With the key on (hands clear of the bore) and then with the engine idling, flex the throttle body and pedal harnesses section by section, including connectors and pass-throughs.
Rock the engine gently (where safe) to stress the harness at engine-to-body transitions.
Note any glitch and the exact location that triggers it.
tests.expected: No glitches or disagreement while the harness is flexed.

outcomes.label: No glitch during the wiggle test
outcomes.interpretation: A harness fault is less likely; continue with circuit and component tests.

outcomes.label: Glitch when a connector is flexed
outcomes.interpretation: Inspect terminal fit and corrosion at that connector and repair.

outcomes.label: Glitch when a harness section is flexed
outcomes.interpretation: Open the harness at that location and repair the damaged wire.

tests.title: Check TSBs, recalls, and calibration updates for throttle control
tests.purpose: Throttle body, pedal, harness, and reduced-power calibration concerns are common bulletin topics.
procedure: Search the OEM service portal by VIN, DTC, and symptom.
Compare the PCM calibration ID with the latest release.
Note any required relearn procedures after repair.
tests.expected: No applicable bulletin, or the bulletin procedure is followed.

outcomes.label: Calibration update applies
outcomes.interpretation: Confirm components test good, then reprogram per the bulletin.

outcomes.label: Bulletin covers the throttle body, pedal, harness, or a cleaning procedure
outcomes.interpretation: Follow the bulletin's confirmation steps before replacing parts.

outcomes.label: No applicable bulletin
outcomes.interpretation: Continue with standard diagnosis.

tests.title: Clean the throttle body per OEM and perform the throttle relearn
tests.purpose: When carbon is found, confirm whether it caused the fault before replacing the throttle body.
procedure: Confirm the OEM permits cleaning this throttle body and which cleaner and method to use; some bores are coated.
With the key off and hands clear of the bore until the key is off, clean the plate edge and bore per the OEM procedure; do not let cleaner enter the sensor or motor housing.
Reinstall the intake duct, clear codes, and perform the OEM throttle and idle relearn.
Recheck commanded vs actual throttle, idle speed, and the sensor pairs.
tests.expected: After cleaning and relearn, actual throttle follows commanded and the fault does not return.

outcomes.label: Fault resolved after cleaning and relearn
outcomes.interpretation: Carbon was the cause; advise the owner and verify on a road test.

outcomes.label: Fault persists after cleaning and relearn
outcomes.interpretation: Carbon was not the cause; continue with motor and sensor circuit tests.

verification: Clear DTCs and perform any OEM throttle or idle relearn required after the repair.
Confirm throttle sensors 1 and 2 and pedal sensors 1 and 2 track smoothly through slow sweeps, and actual throttle follows commanded.
Wiggle-test the repaired harness sections with the engine running and confirm no glitches.
Road test through the freeze-frame conditions (including a cold start if applicable) and confirm full power with no reduced-power message or DTC.

playbooks.title: Idle speed control faults (idle too high, too low, or stalling at stops)
playbooks.summary: Idle speed codes compare actual idle RPM with the PCM's desired idle while the idle control device (IAC valve or electronic throttle) runs out of authority. Use scan data to decide whether the PCM is fighting extra air (vacuum or PCV leaks), too little air (carbon-restricted throttle or IAC passage), a missing relearn, or a desired idle that is raised by a faulty load input or coolant temperature signal. Confirm leaks with smoke and perform the OEM relearn before replacing idle control parts.
clarifyingQuestions: Is the idle too high, too low, surging, or does the engine stall when coming to a stop?
Does the idle change with the A/C on, steering input, headlights or blower on, or when shifting into gear?
Did the problem start after a battery disconnect or replacement, throttle body cleaning, or PCM work?
Is it worse cold, or only after warm-up?
Is there a hissing or whistling noise from the engine bay?

causes.title: Vacuum leak (unmetered air)
causes.description: Air entering through a cracked hose, intake gasket, or brake booster line raises idle speed beyond what the idle control can pull down, and leans the mixture at idle on MAF-based systems.

modifiers.reason: Extra air does not cause low idle
Hoses and gaskets harden with age

causes.title: Carbon-restricted throttle bore or idle air passage
causes.description: Carbon at the throttle plate edge or in the idle air passage restricts idle airflow, so idle sags or stalls at stops, especially when loads come on.

modifiers.reason: Restriction does not cause high idle

causes.title: Idle air control valve failed or sticking (non-electronic-throttle engines)
causes.description: On engines with a separate IAC valve, a failed motor, stuck pintle, or carbon-bound valve cannot regulate bypass air, causing high, low, or surging idle. Not present on electronic-throttle engines.

modifiers.reason: Idle air control system code present

causes.title: Electronic throttle body not controlling idle airflow
causes.description: On electronic-throttle engines the throttle plate controls idle; a weak motor, worn gears, or sensor error prevents accurate small openings.

modifiers.reason: Throttle control or position codes present

causes.title: Idle or throttle relearn not performed
causes.description: After a battery disconnect, throttle cleaning, throttle body replacement, or PCM replacement, many engines need an OEM relearn; without it the learned idle airflow is wrong.

modifiers.reason: Recent event that requires a relearn

causes.title: PCV valve stuck open or PCV hose leak
causes.description: A PCV valve stuck open or a cracked PCV hose adds air at idle, raising idle speed or causing a lean, unstable idle.

causes.title: Faulty engine load input (A/C request, power steering switch, gear range, electrical load)
causes.description: The PCM raises idle or adds air when it sees A/C, steering, gear engagement, or electrical load; a missing input lets idle sag under load, and a stuck input raises desired idle.

modifiers.reason: Idle problem linked to a specific load

causes.title: Coolant temperature sensor reading colder than actual
causes.description: A skewed coolant temperature signal keeps the PCM in cold fast-idle mode, raising desired idle after warm-up.

modifiers.reason: Coolant temperature or thermostat code present

tests.title: Review desired vs actual idle, idle control command, and load inputs
tests.purpose: Decide whether the PCM is fighting extra air, too little air, or a raised desired idle.
procedure: Record DTCs and freeze frame; note coolant temperature, loads, and vehicle speed when the code set.
At fully warm idle with loads off, record desired idle RPM, actual RPM, and the idle control command (IAC position or counts, or throttle opening and idle airflow learn values).
Switch loads on one at a time (A/C, blower, headlights, steering to lock, gear engagement) and watch the command and RPM response.
Compare the coolant temperature PID with actual engine temperature (for example with an infrared thermometer near the sensor).
tests.expected: Actual idle matches desired with the idle control command in its normal range per OEM; desired idle is normal for the operating temperature and loads.
tests.specNote: Desired idle and normal idle control command range per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Actual idle matches desired with a normal command
outcomes.interpretation: The fault is not present now; test under the freeze-frame conditions (cold start, loads, decel to stop).

outcomes.label: Idle above desired while the idle control command is at or near minimum
outcomes.interpretation: Air is entering from somewhere the PCM does not control: smoke test for vacuum and PCV leaks, and check that the throttle plate or IAC fully closes.

outcomes.label: Idle below desired while the idle control command is high or maxed
outcomes.interpretation: Idle air is restricted: inspect the throttle bore and IAC passage for carbon, then check the idle actuator and relearn.

outcomes.label: Desired idle itself is abnormal (load input active or coolant temperature implausible)
outcomes.interpretation: Find the input driving the desired idle: a stuck load input or a coolant temperature signal that disagrees with actual temperature.

tests.title: Compare fuel trims at idle and at a steady higher RPM
tests.purpose: A lean condition at idle that improves at higher RPM points to unmetered air.
procedure: At warm idle, record short-term and long-term fuel trims for each bank.
Hold a steady elevated engine speed in park or neutral (commonly about 2,500 RPM; general guideline — verify against the OEM procedure) and record trims again.
Compare: unmetered air has the largest effect at idle, where total airflow is smallest.
Note that on speed-density (MAP-based) systems a vacuum leak mainly raises idle speed rather than shifting trims.
tests.expected: Total fuel trim near zero at idle and at the higher RPM (general guideline: within roughly ±10% — verify against OEM specification).

outcomes.label: Trims normal at idle and at higher RPM
outcomes.interpretation: Unmetered air is less likely on MAF-based systems.

outcomes.label: Lean at idle, improving at higher RPM
outcomes.interpretation: Unmetered air is likely; smoke test the intake and PCV system.

outcomes.label: Lean at all speeds, or rich
outcomes.interpretation: A fueling or sensor problem beyond idle control is present; diagnose fuel trims separately.

tests.title: Smoke test the intake and PCV system for vacuum leaks
tests.purpose: Locate unmetered air entering the intake.
procedure: With the engine off, seal the intake at the air filter or MAF outlet per the smoke machine instructions.
Introduce smoke into the intake (through a vacuum port or the intake duct) at the machine's intake test setting.
Inspect vacuum hoses, intake gaskets, throttle body gasket, brake booster hose, PCV valve and hoses, and the oil fill cap and dipstick seals.
Remove the equipment and reconnect all hoses.
tests.expected: No smoke escapes from the intake or PCV system.

outcomes.label: No smoke escapes
outcomes.interpretation: No significant intake leak.

outcomes.label: Smoke at a vacuum hose, gasket, or intake component
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the leak and retest idle.

outcomes.label: Smoke at the PCV valve, PCV hoses, oil cap, or dipstick seal
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the PCV leak or replace the stuck PCV valve, then retest idle.

tests.title: Inspect the throttle bore, plate, and IAC passage for carbon
tests.purpose: Carbon restriction is a leading cause of low idle and stalling at stops.
procedure: Key off (keep fingers out of electronic throttle bores whenever the key is on).
Remove the intake duct and inspect the throttle plate edge and bore for carbon or sludge.
On engines with an IAC valve, inspect the IAC pintle and passage for carbon (remove the valve if the OEM procedure allows).
Note the amount and location of deposits.
tests.expected: Throttle plate, bore, and IAC passage free of significant deposits.

outcomes.label: No significant deposits
outcomes.interpretation: Carbon restriction is unlikely.

outcomes.label: Heavy deposits on the plate, bore, or IAC passage
outcomes.interpretation: Clean per the OEM procedure (some bores are coated), perform the relearn, and retest before replacing idle control parts.

tests.title: Command idle RPM (or IAC position) and watch the response
tests.purpose: Verify the idle actuator can both raise and lower idle speed.
procedure: At warm idle, use the scan tool idle RPM control (or IAC position control) to command a higher idle, then a lower idle.
Observe whether RPM follows both commands and how quickly.
Note whether RPM will not come down to the lower command (extra air) or does not respond at all.
Return control to the PCM.
tools: Scan tool with idle RPM or IAC control
tests.expected: RPM follows commanded increases and decreases promptly.

outcomes.label: RPM follows increases and decreases
outcomes.interpretation: The idle actuator works; look at learned values, load inputs, and coolant temperature.

outcomes.label: RPM rises on command but will not come down to the lower target
outcomes.interpretation: Uncontrolled air is entering; smoke test and check that the throttle or IAC closes fully.

outcomes.label: RPM does not respond to commands
outcomes.interpretation: Test the IAC or throttle actuator and its circuit, and check the passage for carbon.

outcomes.label: Idle control function not supported by the scan tool
outcomes.interpretation: Use the scan data review and inspection instead.

tests.title: Verify load input and coolant temperature signals
tests.purpose: Confirm the inputs that set desired idle are correct.
procedure: With the engine warm and idling, watch A/C request and compressor status, power steering pressure input, transmission range, and electrical load PIDs while switching each load on and off.
Confirm each input changes only when its load is applied.
Compare the coolant temperature PID with actual temperature measured near the sensor and with the intake air temperature after an overnight cold soak.
Inspect connectors for any input that is stuck or missing.
tests.expected: Each load input tracks its load, and coolant temperature matches actual temperature.

outcomes.label: All inputs correct
outcomes.interpretation: Desired idle is being set from correct information.

outcomes.label: A load input is stuck on, missing, or does not follow its load
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose that input's switch, sensor, or circuit.

outcomes.label: Coolant temperature reading disagrees with actual temperature
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the coolant temperature sensor and its circuit.

tests.title: Perform the OEM idle or throttle relearn and retest
tests.purpose: Confirm whether missing learned values caused the idle fault.
procedure: Confirm the relearn procedure and its preconditions (temperature, loads off, battery voltage) in service information.
Perform the relearn with the scan tool or the OEM manual procedure.
Retest idle hot and cold, with and without loads, and approaching a stop from speed.
tests.expected: After the relearn, idle matches desired in all conditions.

outcomes.label: Idle normal after relearn
outcomes.interpretation: The missing relearn was the cause; verify on a road test.

outcomes.label: Idle fault persists after relearn
outcomes.interpretation: Continue with airflow and actuator diagnosis.

tests.title: Check TSBs and calibration updates for idle concerns
tests.purpose: Idle calibration updates and cleaning or relearn bulletins are common.
procedure: Search the OEM service portal by VIN, DTC, and symptom (stall at stop, high idle, low idle).
Compare the PCM calibration ID with the latest release.
Note required relearns or revised parts.
tests.expected: No applicable bulletin, or the bulletin procedure is followed.

outcomes.label: Calibration update or relearn bulletin applies
outcomes.interpretation: Perform the bulletin procedure and retest.

outcomes.label: Bulletin covers an idle-related component
outcomes.interpretation: Confirm the condition described in the bulletin before replacing parts.

outcomes.label: No applicable bulletin
outcomes.interpretation: Continue with standard diagnosis.

verification: Clear DTCs and perform the OEM idle or throttle relearn if required.
Confirm actual idle matches desired, cold and hot, with and without loads (A/C, steering, headlights, gear engagement).
Confirm the engine does not stall or dip excessively when coming to a stop from speed.
Road test and confirm the idle control monitor passes with no DTC returning.

playbooks.title: Turbocharger underboost, overboost, and boost sensor faults
playbooks.summary: Boost codes compare actual boost with the PCM's desired boost. Graph desired vs actual boost and the wastegate command first: underboost with the wastegate commanded closed points to a charge-air leak, a wastegate that will not close, intake or exhaust restriction, or a worn turbocharger, while overboost points to the wastegate or its control, or a sensor that misreads. Pressure-test the charge-air system and check the wastegate and boost sensor before replacing a turbocharger, and remember that turbochargers and exhaust parts stay extremely hot after shutdown.
clarifyingQuestions: Does the low power occur only under higher load, and does boost build normally at first and then fall off?
Is there a whistle, hiss, or whoosh under boost, or a siren, whine, or grinding noise from the turbocharger?
Is there blue or gray exhaust smoke, oil consumption, or excessive oil in the intake ducting?
Any recent intercooler, intake, or turbocharger work, or charge-air hoses that have come off before?
Is a wastegate rattle heard at cold start or over bumps?

causes.title: Charge-air leak (hose, coupler, clamp, intercooler, or bypass valve)
causes.description: Pressurized air escapes through a split hose, loose clamp, cracked intercooler, or leaking bypass (diverter) valve, so boost cannot reach the desired value; a hiss or whistle under load is common.

modifiers.reason: Couplers and hoses degrade with heat and oil exposure

causes.title: Wastegate stuck, binding, or with a failed actuator
causes.description: A wastegate stuck open bypasses exhaust around the turbine (underboost); stuck closed, it cannot limit boost (overboost). Worn bushings or linkage and failed vacuum, pressure, or electric actuators are common.

causes.title: Boost (wastegate) control solenoid or its control hoses
causes.description: On pneumatic wastegate systems the PCM regulates actuator pressure or vacuum through a control solenoid; a sticking solenoid or a cracked, misrouted control hose causes underboost or overboost.

causes.title: Worn or damaged turbocharger
causes.description: Bearing wear, excessive shaft play, or damaged compressor or turbine wheels reduce boost and can cause whine, siren noise, and oil smoke. Oil supply or contamination problems often cause the failure and must be corrected too.

modifiers.reason: Turbocharger noise or oil smoke reported

causes.title: Boost pressure sensor skewed or erratic
causes.description: A skewed or erratic boost pressure sensor makes the PCM control to the wrong pressure and can set range/performance, underboost, or overboost codes.

modifiers.reason: A sensor reading low can drive overboost

causes.title: Exhaust restriction (plugged converter or damaged exhaust)
causes.description: A restricted converter or crushed pipe downstream of the turbine raises backpressure, reducing turbine efficiency and power.

causes.title: Air intake restriction (filter or inlet duct)
causes.description: A clogged air filter, collapsed inlet duct, or snow or debris blockage starves the compressor and reduces boost.

causes.title: Boost sensor or boost control wiring fault
causes.description: Heat-damaged or chafed wiring to the boost sensor, control solenoid, or electric wastegate actuator causes erratic readings or loss of boost control.

modifiers.reason: Boost sensor or wastegate circuit code present

causes.title: Boost control calibration issue
causes.description: OEMs sometimes revise boost control and diagnostic thresholds to correct false underboost or overboost detection.

tests.title: Graph desired vs actual boost, wastegate command, and boost sensor at key on
tests.purpose: Characterize the boost fault (underboost, overboost, or sensor error) without disassembly.
procedure: Record DTCs and freeze frame; note RPM, load, and boost when the code set.
Key on, engine off: compare the boost pressure sensor with the barometric pressure PID; they should agree closely per the OEM description.
On a dynamometer, or on a safe road with a helper operating the scan tool, graph desired boost, actual boost, and wastegate command during a moderate and a full-load acceleration within legal limits.
Note whether actual boost falls short while the wastegate is commanded fully closed, overshoots while it is commanded open, or reads implausibly.
tests.expected: Boost sensor agrees with barometric pressure at key on, and actual boost tracks desired with the wastegate command in its normal range.
tests.specNote: Desired boost behavior and wastegate command range per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Actual boost tracks desired and the sensor is plausible
outcomes.interpretation: Not reproduced; repeat under the freeze-frame conditions (temperature, altitude, load).

outcomes.label: Actual boost below desired with the wastegate commanded closed
outcomes.interpretation: Pressure-test the charge-air system first, then check the wastegate, intake and exhaust restriction, and the turbocharger.

outcomes.label: Actual boost above desired with the wastegate commanded open
outcomes.interpretation: Check wastegate movement, the control solenoid and hoses, and the boost sensor reading.

outcomes.label: Boost sensor disagrees with baro at key on, or reads erratically
outcomes.interpretation: Test the boost sensor and its circuit.

tests.title: Pressure-test the charge-air system
tests.purpose: Locate boost leaks in hoses, couplers, the intercooler, and the bypass valve.
procedure: Engine off. Install the boost leak tester adapter at the compressor inlet (or the OEM-specified point) and block the path as the tester instructions describe.
Secure all adapters so they cannot blow off; wear eye protection.
Apply regulated shop air at a low pressure that does not exceed normal boost or the tester's recommended setting.
Listen and spray soapy water (or add smoke) at hoses, couplers, clamps, the intercooler core and end tanks, the throttle body, and the bypass valve.
Release pressure before removing the adapters.
tools: Soapy water spray or smoke machine
tests.expected: The system holds pressure with no audible or visible leaks.

outcomes.label: System holds pressure with no leaks
outcomes.interpretation: No charge-air leak; check the wastegate, restrictions, and the turbocharger.

outcomes.label: Leak at a hose, coupler, clamp, or throttle body seal
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the damaged hose or coupler and clamp; retest.

outcomes.label: Leak at the intercooler core or end tanks
outcomes.interpretation: Repair or replace the intercooler and check it for oil contamination.

outcomes.label: Leak through the bypass (diverter) valve
outcomes.interpretation: Test and replace the bypass valve or its diaphragm as needed.

tests.title: Check wastegate actuator and linkage movement
tests.purpose: Confirm the wastegate moves freely and its actuator works.
procedure: Allow the turbocharger and exhaust to cool; they stay extremely hot long after shutdown.
Pneumatic actuators: apply the controlled pressure or vacuum the OEM specifies with a hand pump and confirm the rod moves smoothly and the actuator holds.
Electric actuators: command the wastegate through its range with the scan tool and compare commanded and actual position.
Check the linkage and bushing for binding, excessive play, or rattle.
tests.expected: Smooth, full wastegate travel with no binding or excessive play; the actuator holds pressure or reaches the commanded position.
tests.specNote: Actuator test pressure and travel per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Wastegate and actuator move freely and correctly
outcomes.interpretation: The wastegate is mechanically sound; check its control and other causes.

outcomes.label: Wastegate or linkage binding, seized, or with excessive play
outcomes.interpretation: Repair per the OEM procedure; on many designs the wastegate is serviced with the turbocharger.

outcomes.label: Actuator leaks or does not reach commanded position
outcomes.interpretation: Check the actuator circuit (electric) before replacing the actuator.

tests.title: Boost control solenoid, control hose, and circuit test
tests.purpose: Separate a failed control solenoid or control hose from wiring faults.
procedure: Inspect the control hoses for cracks, splits, and correct routing per the OEM diagram.
Measure the solenoid winding resistance and compare with the OEM specification.
Command the solenoid with the scan tool and verify the control signal at the connector with a lab scope or test light.
Apply pressure or vacuum through the solenoid with a hand pump and confirm it switches flow when commanded.
tests.expected: Hoses intact and correctly routed, winding within specification, and the solenoid switches flow on command.
tests.specNote: Solenoid resistance and hose routing per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Solenoid, hoses, and circuit good
outcomes.interpretation: Boost control is working; check the wastegate and turbocharger.

outcomes.label: Solenoid does not switch, leaks, or winding out of specification
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the control solenoid and retest boost.

outcomes.label: Control hose cracked, disconnected, or misrouted
outcomes.interpretation: Replace or reroute the hose per the OEM diagram.

outcomes.label: Open, short, or missing command in the circuit
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the wiring and retest.

tests.title: Inspect the compressor wheel, shaft play, and oil in the intake
tests.purpose: Confirm or rule out turbocharger damage before replacement.
procedure: Engine off and cool. Never run the engine with the intake duct removed.
Remove the inlet duct at the compressor and inspect the compressor wheel for damaged, bent, or eroded blades and signs of rubbing on the housing.
Check shaft play by hand per the OEM criteria (some radial play is normal; axial play and wheel contact are not).
Check the inlet and charge pipes for excessive oil and inspect the oil supply and drain lines.
Inspect the air filter and inlet duct for damage that could have admitted debris.
tests.expected: Compressor wheel undamaged with no housing contact, shaft play within OEM criteria, and no excessive oil.
tests.specNote: Shaft play criteria per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: No damage, normal play, no excessive oil
outcomes.interpretation: The turbocharger is unlikely to be the cause.

outcomes.label: Blade damage, housing contact, or excessive shaft play
outcomes.interpretation: The turbocharger is damaged. Find the root cause (oil supply, contamination, debris ingestion) before replacement.

outcomes.label: Excessive oil in the inlet or charge pipes
outcomes.interpretation: Check for turbo seal leakage, drain restriction, or crankcase ventilation problems.

tests.title: Boost pressure sensor plausibility and circuit test
tests.purpose: Confirm the boost sensor reads correctly and its circuit is sound.
procedure: Key on, engine off: compare the boost sensor PID with barometric pressure.
Back-probe the sensor and measure reference voltage, ground drop, and signal; compare with the scan tool.
With the sensor removed or teed per the OEM procedure, apply a known pressure with a hand pump and gauge and confirm the reading follows.
Wiggle-test the harness while monitoring the signal.
tests.expected: Matches baro at key on, follows applied pressure, and circuits are within the OEM specification.
tests.specNote: Sensor transfer function and circuit values per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Sensor and circuit good
outcomes.interpretation: The boost reading can be trusted.

outcomes.label: Offset from baro or does not follow applied pressure
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the sensor after confirming the circuit.

outcomes.label: Reference, ground, or signal circuit fault
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the circuit and retest.

tests.title: Check intake and exhaust restriction
tests.purpose: Rule out a starved compressor or a restricted exhaust.
procedure: Inspect the air filter and inlet duct for clogging, collapse, snow, or debris.
Measure exhaust backpressure by the OEM method (for example, a backpressure gauge in an oxygen sensor port downstream of the turbine) at idle and at a steady elevated engine speed.
Allow exhaust components to cool before installing or removing test equipment; keep hoses clear of hot surfaces.
Inspect the exhaust for crushed pipes or a rattling converter.
tests.expected: Clean air filter and inlet; backpressure within the OEM specification.
tests.specNote: Backpressure limits per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: No intake or exhaust restriction
outcomes.interpretation: Restriction is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Air filter or inlet restricted
outcomes.interpretation: Correct the restriction and inspect the compressor for debris damage.

outcomes.label: Excessive exhaust backpressure
outcomes.interpretation: Locate the restriction and find why the converter failed (misfire, oil or coolant consumption) before replacing it.

tests.title: Check TSBs, recalls, and calibration updates for boost concerns
tests.purpose: Revised couplers, wastegate components, and boost calibrations are common bulletin topics.
procedure: Search the OEM service portal by VIN, DTC, and symptom.
Compare the PCM calibration ID with the latest release.
Check powertrain warranty coverage for turbocharger components.
tests.expected: No applicable bulletin, or the bulletin procedure is followed.

outcomes.label: Boost control calibration update applies
outcomes.interpretation: Confirm the hardware is sound, then reprogram per the bulletin.

outcomes.label: Bulletin covers a charge-air, wastegate, sensor, or turbocharger component
outcomes.interpretation: Follow the bulletin's confirmation steps before replacing parts.

outcomes.label: No applicable bulletin
outcomes.interpretation: Continue with standard diagnosis.

verification: Clear DTCs and road test with a helper operating the scan tool (or use a dynamometer) under the freeze-frame conditions.
Confirm actual boost tracks desired through acceleration without overshoot, with the wastegate command in its normal range.
Re-pressure-test the charge-air system after any hose, coupler, or intercooler repair.
Confirm no abnormal turbocharger noise or smoke and no DTC returns.

playbooks.title: Vehicle speed sensor signal faults
playbooks.summary: Vehicle speed sensor codes mean the PCM's vehicle speed input is missing, implausible, or erratic compared with engine load and other speed sources. Identify where this vehicle gets its speed signal (a transmission output sensor, ABS wheel speed sensors shared over the network, or both), compare every available speed source in scan data, then test the sensor signal, wiring, and tone ring before replacing a sensor or module. Incorrect tire size or configuration causes speed range/performance faults without any failed part.
clarifyingQuestions: Does the speedometer work, drop out, or read erratically, and does it agree with GPS speed?
Are ABS, traction control, or stability warnings on, or are ABS or network codes stored in other modules?
Have the tires, wheels, axle ratio, or ride height been changed from the factory configuration?
Does the transmission shift erratically or stay in one gear, and is cruise control inoperative?
Does the problem occur only at certain speeds, over bumps, or in wet weather?

causes.title: Failed vehicle speed or transmission output speed sensor
causes.description: A failed sensor produces no signal, a weak signal at low speed, or dropouts; metallic debris on a magnetic sensor tip and internal breaks are common.

modifiers.reason: Output speed sensor code also present
Shift quality affected by missing speed input

causes.title: Speed sensor wiring damage
causes.description: Speed sensor wiring near the transmission, exhaust, or suspension is exposed to heat, chafing, and flexing, causing opens, shorts, or noise pickup.

modifiers.reason: Circuit low or intermittent/erratic code present

causes.title: Faulty ABS wheel speed sensor (where vehicle speed is derived from wheel speeds)
causes.description: Many vehicles calculate vehicle speed from ABS wheel speed sensors and share it over the network; a failed or erratic wheel sensor corrupts the vehicle speed signal and usually sets ABS codes.

modifiers.reason: ABS, traction, or stability warning reported

causes.title: Corroded or loose speed sensor connector
causes.description: Underbody connectors exposed to water and salt corrode, causing intermittent or low-amplitude signals.

modifiers.reason: Circuit low or intermittent/erratic code present

causes.title: Damaged, cracked, or contaminated tone (reluctor) ring
causes.description: A cracked, corroded, or debris-packed tone ring on the output shaft, axle, or hub produces an erratic signal that worsens with speed.

causes.title: ABS module not providing vehicle speed
causes.description: Where the ABS module calculates and broadcasts vehicle speed, an internal fault or loss of its network message removes the speed input.

modifiers.reason: ABS, traction, or stability warning reported
Lost communication with the ABS module

causes.title: Incorrect tire size, axle ratio, or configuration
causes.description: Non-factory tire sizes or an incorrect tire size or axle ratio setting makes vehicle speed disagree with other speed sources and the speedometer read incorrectly.

modifiers.reason: Tire, gearing, or speedometer accuracy concern

causes.title: Network (CAN) fault preventing speed data sharing
causes.description: Where vehicle speed is shared between modules over the network, bus wiring faults or a module disrupting the bus remove or corrupt the speed message.

tests.title: Compare all vehicle speed sources in scan data
tests.purpose: Find which speed source drops out or disagrees: the vehicle speed input, transmission output speed, or individual wheel speeds.
procedure: Record DTCs from all modules and the freeze frame, including vehicle speed when the code set.
From service information, identify the source of the PCM's vehicle speed signal on this vehicle.
On a road test (with a helper operating the scan tool) or on a lift with the drive wheels safely supported, graph PCM vehicle speed, transmission output speed, and all four wheel speeds.
Compare the readings with GPS speed on a road test, noting dropouts, spikes, or a consistent proportional error.
tools: Scan tool with graphing and ABS access
Lift or helper for road test
tests.expected: All speed sources agree with each other and with GPS speed throughout the speed range, with no dropouts.

outcomes.label: All sources agree and match GPS
outcomes.interpretation: Not reproduced; perform a wiggle test and repeat under the freeze-frame conditions.

outcomes.label: Vehicle speed or output speed drops out or is erratic while wheel speeds stay valid
outcomes.interpretation: Test the vehicle or output speed sensor signal, wiring, and connector.

outcomes.label: One or more wheel speeds erratic or dropping out
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the affected wheel speed sensor, its wiring, and its tone ring.

outcomes.label: All sources consistent with each other but proportionally off from GPS
outcomes.interpretation: Check tire size and configuration against the build data.

outcomes.label: Vehicle speed missing in the PCM with network or ABS communication problems
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the ABS module and the network before the sensors.

tests.title: Inspect the speed sensor, connector, wiring, and mounting
tests.purpose: Find damaged wiring, loose or contaminated sensors, and visible tone ring damage.
procedure: Safely raise and support the vehicle.
Inspect the speed sensor (and suspect wheel speed sensors) for secure mounting, cracked housings, and metallic debris on the tip.
Trace the wiring for chafing, heat damage near the exhaust, stretched sections at suspension points, and previous repairs.
Inspect connectors for corrosion and terminal fit, and visible tone rings for cracks, missing teeth, or packed debris.
tools: Lift or jack and jack stands
tests.expected: Sensor secure and clean, wiring and connectors intact, and tone ring undamaged.

outcomes.label: No visible faults
outcomes.interpretation: Continue with signal testing.

outcomes.label: Damaged wiring or corroded connector
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the wiring or connector and retest.

outcomes.label: Loose, cracked, or debris-covered sensor, or damaged tone ring
outcomes.interpretation: Clean or secure the sensor, or repair the tone ring, then retest; replace the sensor only if its signal remains faulty.

tests.title: Test the speed sensor signal with the drive wheels spinning
tests.purpose: Confirm whether the sensor produces a clean signal and whether its supply and ground are intact.
procedure: Safely raise and support the vehicle so the drive wheels are off the ground; keep clear of rotating wheels and driveline.
Identify the sensor type from service information (passive magnetic or active/Hall with supply and ground).
Passive sensors: measure winding resistance with the sensor unplugged and compare with the OEM specification.
Active sensors: verify supply voltage and ground at the connector with the key on.
With the wheels turning slowly in gear, capture the signal on a lab scope and look for amplitude, missing pulses, or dropouts as speed changes.
tests.expected: A clean, regular signal whose frequency rises with speed and whose amplitude (passive sensors) grows with speed; supply and ground within the OEM specification.
tests.specNote: Sensor type, resistance, supply voltage, and signal characteristics per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Clean signal and good supply and ground
outcomes.interpretation: The sensor works at the connector; check the circuit to the module and the module input.

outcomes.label: No signal or abnormally weak signal with good supply and ground
outcomes.interpretation: Check the sensor tip for debris and the mounting for correct position; if both are good, the sensor is faulty.

outcomes.label: Missing pulses or dropouts that repeat with shaft rotation
outcomes.interpretation: A pattern that repeats once per revolution points to the tone ring; random dropouts point to wiring or the sensor.

outcomes.label: Active sensor missing supply or ground
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the supply or ground circuit and retest.

tests.title: Wiggle test the speed sensor harness while monitoring speed
tests.purpose: Reproduce intermittent dropouts caused by wiring or connectors.
procedure: With the drive wheels safely supported and turning slowly in gear (or on a careful road test with a helper), graph the vehicle speed PID or the sensor signal.
Keeping hands clear of rotating parts, flex the harness and connector section by section.
Note any dropout and the exact location that triggers it.
tools: Scan tool with graphing or lab scope
tests.expected: No dropout while the harness is flexed.

outcomes.label: No dropout during the wiggle test
outcomes.interpretation: A harness fault is less likely.

outcomes.label: Dropout when a connector is flexed
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the connector terminals or seals.

outcomes.label: Dropout when a harness section is flexed
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the damaged section of wiring.

tests.title: Check ABS module codes and network communication
tests.purpose: Where vehicle speed comes from the ABS module, confirm that module and the network are delivering it.
procedure: Perform a full-vehicle code scan and record ABS and network (U) codes.
Confirm the PCM (and TCM, cluster) communicate with the ABS module and receive a valid vehicle speed message.
Review ABS module wheel speed sensor codes and their freeze-frame data.
If communication codes are present, follow the OEM network diagnostic procedure.
tests.expected: No ABS or network codes, and all modules receive a valid vehicle speed.

outcomes.label: No ABS or network faults
outcomes.interpretation: The ABS and network side is healthy; focus on the vehicle or output speed sensor circuit.

outcomes.label: ABS module stores a wheel speed sensor code
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the wheel speed sensor circuit named by the ABS code first.

outcomes.label: ABS module internal fault or no speed broadcast
outcomes.interpretation: Verify ABS module power and ground before condemning the module; follow the OEM procedure.

outcomes.label: Lost communication or network codes
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the network per the OEM procedure before replacing sensors.

tests.title: Verify tire size, axle ratio, and speed calibration configuration
tests.purpose: Confirm the speed calculation matches the vehicle's actual tires and gearing.
procedure: Compare the installed tire size with the door placard and build data; check for mismatched tire sizes between axles.
Read the configured tire size and axle ratio in the relevant modules with the scan tool.
Compare with the vehicle's build data or OEM configuration record.
If changed intentionally, reconfigure per the OEM procedure where permitted.
tools: Build data or OEM configuration record
tests.expected: Installed tires and configured values match the build data.

outcomes.label: Tires and configuration match
outcomes.interpretation: Configuration is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Tire size or configuration does not match
outcomes.interpretation: Correct the tires or the configuration per the OEM procedure and recheck against GPS speed.

tests.title: Check TSBs and recalls for speed sensor concerns
tests.purpose: Sensor, harness routing, and configuration bulletins are common for speed signal faults.
procedure: Search the OEM service portal by VIN, DTC, and symptom.
Review harness routing or connector bulletins for the speed sensor location.
Note any module software or configuration updates.
tests.expected: No applicable bulletin, or the bulletin procedure is followed.

outcomes.label: Bulletin covers a sensor, harness, connector, or module
outcomes.interpretation: Follow the bulletin's confirmation steps before replacing parts.

outcomes.label: Software or configuration update applies
outcomes.interpretation: Perform the update per the bulletin and retest.

outcomes.label: No applicable bulletin
outcomes.interpretation: Continue with standard diagnosis.

verification: Clear DTCs in all modules.
Road test and confirm the PCM vehicle speed, wheel speeds, output speed, and speedometer agree with each other and with GPS speed across the speed range.
Confirm normal shifting and cruise control operation with no ABS, traction, or stability warnings.
Confirm no DTC returns after a drive covering the freeze-frame speed range.

playbooks.title: Rough idle without stored codes
playbooks.summary: A rough idle without stored codes is diagnosed by first separating true combustion problems from normal engine vibration transmitted through worn mounts. Misfire counters and fuel trims then show whether the problem is confined to one cylinder (ignition, injector, compression) or affects all cylinders (vacuum or PCV leaks, EGR flow at idle, a dirty throttle, intake valve deposits). Confirm each suspect with a targeted test before replacing parts.
clarifyingQuestions: Is the idle uneven and stumbling (combustion), or smooth-sounding with vibration felt in the body, especially in gear?
Is it worse cold, after warm-up, with the A/C on, or in gear?
Are there any pending codes, or has the MIL ever flashed?
Is the engine direct injected, and what are the mileage and spark plug replacement history?
Has there been recent work on the intake, ignition system, or engine mounts?

causes.title: Vacuum leak
causes.description: Unmetered air leans the mixture most at idle, where total airflow is lowest, causing a lean, uneven idle across several cylinders.

modifiers.reason: Gasket and hose leaks can be worse cold
Hoses and gaskets harden with age

causes.title: Worn or fouled spark plugs
causes.description: Worn electrodes and fouling raise the required firing voltage and cause intermittent misfires that are most noticeable at idle.

modifiers.reason: Plugs may be past their service interval

causes.title: Weak ignition coil
causes.description: A coil with internal breakdown or boot tracking misfires one cylinder, often worse in damp weather or under load.

causes.title: Restricted or leaking fuel injector
causes.description: A clogged injector leans one cylinder and a leaking injector floods it; either causes a single-cylinder idle misfire.

causes.title: Carbon-restricted throttle body
causes.description: Carbon restricts idle airflow so idle becomes low and unstable, often worse with the A/C on or in gear.

causes.title: Worn or collapsed engine or transmission mount
causes.description: A failed mount transmits normal idle vibration into the body, so a smooth-running engine feels rough, typically worse in gear.

modifiers.reason: Worse in gear or clunk on engagement

causes.title: EGR valve leaking or stuck open at idle
causes.description: Exhaust gas admitted at idle dilutes the charge and causes a rough idle or stalling that improves when the EGR valve is blocked.

causes.title: PCV valve stuck open or PCV hose leak
causes.description: Excess crankcase ventilation flow or a cracked PCV hose adds unmetered air at idle.

causes.title: Low compression in one or more cylinders
causes.description: A burnt valve, worn rings, or a head gasket leak lowers cylinder pressure and produces a steady misfire at idle.

causes.title: Intake valve carbon deposits (common on direct-injection engines)
causes.description: Without fuel washing the intake valves, direct-injection engines build carbon that disturbs airflow and sealing, causing rough idle and cold-start misfire.

tests.title: Review pending codes, misfire counters, Mode $06, and fuel trims at idle
tests.purpose: Decide whether the roughness is combustion related, and whether it is confined to one cylinder or affects all cylinders.
procedure: Check all modules for pending and history codes.
