At warm idle, and cold if the complaint is cold, record current misfire counters for each cylinder and review Mode $06 misfire results.
Record short-term and long-term fuel trims at idle and at a steady elevated speed.
Repeat in gear with the brakes firmly applied and with the A/C on, if safe, noting any change.
tools: Scan tool with misfire counters and Mode $06
tests.expected: Misfire counts at or near zero on all cylinders and fuel trims near zero (general guideline: total within roughly ±10% — verify against OEM specification).

outcomes.label: No meaningful misfire counts and normal trims
outcomes.interpretation: Combustion looks healthy; check engine mounts and idle airflow.

outcomes.label: Misfire counts concentrated on one cylinder
outcomes.interpretation: Test that cylinder's ignition, injector, and compression.

outcomes.label: Misfire across several cylinders and/or lean trims at idle
outcomes.interpretation: Look for causes common to all cylinders: vacuum or PCV leaks, EGR flow at idle, worn plugs, or intake deposits.

tests.title: Inspect engine and transmission mounts
tests.purpose: Determine whether a smooth-running engine's vibration is being transmitted through failed mounts.
procedure: Visually inspect all engine and transmission mounts for torn rubber, collapse, fluid leakage (hydraulic mounts), or contact between metal parts.
With a helper firmly holding the brakes, the hood open, and nobody in front of or behind the vehicle, briefly shift between drive and reverse at idle and watch for excessive engine movement.
Compare vibration in park or neutral with vibration in gear.
Check for exhaust or engine components contacting the body.
tools: Pry bar (for movement check with the engine off)
tests.expected: Mounts intact with only slight engine movement during engagement and no metal-to-metal contact.

outcomes.label: Mounts in good condition
outcomes.interpretation: Mounts are not the cause.

outcomes.label: Torn, collapsed, or leaking mount, or excessive engine movement
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the failed mount and recheck; a failed mount can also be a result of a severe misfire, so confirm combustion is healthy.

tests.title: Smoke test the intake and PCV system
tests.purpose: Locate unmetered air entering the intake.
procedure: With the engine off, seal the intake at the air filter or MAF outlet per the smoke machine instructions.
Introduce smoke into the intake at the machine's intake test setting.
Inspect vacuum hoses, intake and throttle body gaskets, brake booster hose, PCV valve and hoses, and the oil fill cap and dipstick seals.
Remove the equipment and reconnect all hoses.
tests.expected: No smoke escapes from the intake or PCV system.

outcomes.label: No smoke escapes
outcomes.interpretation: No significant intake leak.

outcomes.label: Smoke at a vacuum hose, gasket, or intake component
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the leak and recheck idle quality and trims.

outcomes.label: Smoke at the PCV valve, PCV hoses, oil cap, or dipstick seal
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the PCV leak or replace the stuck PCV valve and recheck.

tests.title: Inspect spark plugs and test ignition coils
tests.purpose: Confirm or rule out worn plugs and a weak coil on the misfiring cylinder.
procedure: Engine off: remove the ignition coils and plugs from the suspect cylinder(s), or all cylinders if misfire is random.
Inspect plugs for electrode wear, gap, fouling (fuel, oil, or coolant), and cracked insulators; compare with the others.
Inspect coil boots for carbon tracking or cracks.
Swap the suspect coil to another cylinder, or view secondary ignition with a scope, and see whether the misfire follows the coil.
Reinstall plugs tightened to the OEM specification.
tools: Spark plug socket and torque wrench
Ignition scope or secondary ignition probe (optional)
tests.expected: Plugs within service condition and gap, clean boots, and misfire that does not follow the coil.
tests.specNote: Plug type, gap, and tightening torque per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Plugs and coils good
outcomes.interpretation: Ignition is unlikely; test the injector and compression on the affected cylinder.

outcomes.label: Plugs worn, incorrectly gapped, or fouled
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the plugs; fuel, oil, or coolant fouling indicates an underlying cause that must be found.

outcomes.label: Misfire follows the coil, or weak secondary output
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the coil and inspect its boot and the plug.

tests.title: Test the injector on the weak cylinder
tests.purpose: Confirm whether a restricted or leaking injector is causing a single-cylinder misfire.
procedure: Compare injector current waveforms for all cylinders with a low-amp probe; look for an abnormal pintle signature on the suspect cylinder.
Port injection: perform an injector balance (pressure drop) test per the OEM procedure, relieving and restoring fuel pressure safely with fire precautions in place.
Direct injection: use the OEM injector tests or cylinder contribution data only; do not open the high-pressure system.
Compare results with the other cylinders.
tools: Fuel pressure gauge and injector pulser (port injection)
tests.expected: The suspect injector's waveform and flow match the others.
tests.specNote: Balance test method and allowable variation per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Injector matches the others
outcomes.interpretation: The injector is unlikely to be the cause.

outcomes.label: Abnormal waveform, low flow, or leakage on the suspect injector
outcomes.interpretation: Service or replace the injector per the OEM procedure and recheck misfire counters.

tests.title: Relative and cranking compression test, with leak-down if low
tests.purpose: Confirm or rule out low compression on the weak cylinder.
procedure: Perform a relative compression test with a lab scope and current probe on the starter circuit, or a cranking compression test with ignition and fuel disabled per the OEM procedure.
Compare cylinders with each other and with the OEM specification.
If a cylinder is low, perform a cylinder leak-down test and listen at the intake, exhaust, oil fill, and coolant reservoir to locate the leak.
Reinstall plugs and coils, tightened to the OEM specification.
tests.expected: Compression even across cylinders and within the OEM specification.
tests.specNote: Compression specification and allowable variation per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Compression even and within specification
outcomes.interpretation: Mechanical causes are unlikely.

outcomes.label: One or more cylinders low
outcomes.interpretation: Use the leak-down results to identify valves, rings, or a head gasket before planning repairs.

tests.title: Check for EGR flow at idle
tests.purpose: Determine whether exhaust gas is entering at idle through a leaking or stuck EGR valve.
procedure: At warm idle, confirm EGR is commanded closed in scan data.
Observe the EGR position PID where available; it should indicate closed.
Temporarily block EGR flow per the OEM procedure (or disconnect the valve where the OEM permits) and note any change in idle quality.
Restore the system and clear any codes set by the test.
tools: Block-off plate or OEM tool as specified
tests.expected: No change in idle quality when EGR is blocked.

outcomes.label: Idle unchanged when EGR is blocked
outcomes.interpretation: EGR is not flowing at idle.

outcomes.label: Idle smooths when EGR is blocked
outcomes.interpretation: The EGR valve is leaking or stuck open; inspect for carbon on the seat.

outcomes.label: Engine has no external EGR valve
outcomes.interpretation: Not applicable; internal EGR is controlled by valve timing.

tests.title: Inspect the throttle body for carbon
tests.purpose: Carbon restriction causes low, unstable idle.
procedure: Key off; keep fingers out of electronic throttle bores whenever the key is on.
Remove the intake duct and inspect the throttle plate edge and bore for deposits.
If deposits are heavy, clean per the OEM procedure (some bores are coated) and perform the idle relearn.
Recheck idle quality.
tests.expected: Plate and bore free of significant deposits.

outcomes.label: No significant deposits
outcomes.interpretation: Throttle deposits are not the cause.

outcomes.label: Heavy deposits found
outcomes.interpretation: Clean, relearn, and recheck idle quality before other repairs.

tests.title: Borescope inspection of intake valves for carbon
tests.purpose: Confirm intake valve deposits on direct-injection engines before recommending cleaning.
procedure: With the engine cool, gain access to the intake ports per the OEM procedure (for example through an intake runner or sensor opening, or with the intake manifold removed).
Rotate the engine by hand so each intake valve is closed before inspecting.
Inspect the valve tulips and ports with a borescope and compare the deposit level between cylinders.
Reassemble with new gaskets as required.
tests.expected: Only light, even deposits on the intake valves.

outcomes.label: Light or normal deposits
outcomes.interpretation: Intake deposits are not the cause.

outcomes.label: Heavy carbon on the intake valves
outcomes.interpretation: Clean the valves by the OEM-approved method and check for bulletins on causes such as PCV oil carryover.

verification: Confirm misfire counters remain at or near zero on all cylinders at idle, cold and hot.
Confirm idle fuel trims are near zero (general guideline: total within roughly ±10% — verify against OEM specification).
Confirm the idle feels smooth in park and in gear, with the A/C on and off.
Road test and recheck for pending codes.

playbooks.title: Hesitation, stumble, bog, or flat spot on acceleration
playbooks.summary: Hesitation complaints are diagnosed by reproducing the event while recording data and then classifying it: a lean excursion (airflow measurement, fuel pressure, injectors, vacuum leaks), a misfire under load (coils, plugs), a sluggish response without lean or misfire (throttle deposits, exhaust restriction, calibration), or torque converter clutch shudder mistaken for an engine problem. Confirm the category with targeted tests before replacing parts.
clarifyingQuestions: Does it happen when pulling away from a stop, when passing or climbing, or at light steady cruise?
Is it worse cold, hot, or in wet weather?
Does it feel like a misfire (jerk or buck), a flat spot with no power, or a vibration like driving over rumble strips?
Has the MIL flashed, or are there pending codes?
When were the spark plugs, air filter, and fuel filter last serviced, and is an oiled aftermarket air filter installed?

causes.title: Contaminated mass airflow sensor
causes.description: A contaminated sensing element under-reports airflow, especially during rapid throttle opening, so the engine goes lean and stumbles.

modifiers.reason: MAF circuit or range code present

causes.title: Low fuel pressure or volume under load
causes.description: A weak pump, restricted filter, or regulator fault lets pressure sag when demand rises, leaning the mixture during acceleration.

modifiers.reason: Worse under high load or when hot

causes.title: Ignition coil breaking down under load
causes.description: Higher cylinder pressure under load raises the voltage needed to fire the plug; a weak coil or tracked boot misfires, felt as a jerk or buck.

causes.title: Worn or incorrectly gapped spark plugs
causes.description: Worn electrodes increase the required firing voltage, causing load misfires and a stumble on acceleration.

modifiers.reason: Plugs may be past their service interval

causes.title: Restricted fuel injectors
causes.description: Deposits reduce injector flow so the engine runs lean under high demand even with normal fuel pressure.

causes.title: Vacuum leak
causes.description: Unmetered air leans the mixture at light load and tip-in, producing a stumble when pulling away.

causes.title: Carbon at the throttle plate (tip-in dead spot)
causes.description: Deposits at the plate edge distort airflow just off idle, causing a dead spot or delayed response when pulling away.

causes.title: Exhaust restriction (plugged converter)
causes.description: A restricted converter limits airflow at higher RPM and load, producing a bog and lack of power that worsens as speed rises.

modifiers.reason: Misfire history can damage the converter

causes.title: Torque converter clutch shudder (TCC apply control, fluid, or converter)
causes.description: Shudder during torque converter clutch apply at light cruise feels like an engine stumble or rumble-strip vibration while engine data stays normal.

modifiers.reason: Symptom pattern typical of TCC shudder

causes.title: Drivability calibration issue
causes.description: OEMs issue calibration updates for tip-in hesitation, torque management, and shift or throttle response concerns on otherwise healthy engines.

tests.title: Reproduce the event on a road test with data recording
tests.purpose: Classify the stumble as lean, misfire, sluggish response, or torque converter shudder.
procedure: Check for pending codes and review any freeze frame data.

Set up recording of RPM, load, MAF, throttle and pedal position, short-term fuel trims, O2 or A/F sensor signals, fuel pressure (if available), misfire counters, and torque converter clutch command and slip.
With a helper operating the scan tool, reproduce the complaint on a safe road within legal limits (tip-in from a stop, passing, light cruise), and mark the event.
Review the recording around the marked event: lean excursion, misfire counts, slow response without lean or misfire, or TCC slip oscillation.
tests.expected: No lean excursions, no misfire counts, prompt engine response, and stable TCC operation during the maneuvers that trigger the complaint.

outcomes.label: O2/A-F goes lean and trims spike positive during the stumble
outcomes.interpretation: Fuel delivery or airflow measurement is suspect: check MAF plausibility, fuel pressure under load, injectors, and leaks.

outcomes.label: Misfire counters increment during the stumble
outcomes.interpretation: Ignition under load is the prime suspect; check coils and plugs on the affected cylinders.

outcomes.label: Bog or flat spot reproduced with no lean excursion or misfire
outcomes.interpretation: Look at throttle response and deposits, exhaust restriction, and calibration updates.

outcomes.label: TCC applied with oscillating slip; engine data normal
outcomes.interpretation: The complaint is torque converter clutch shudder; diagnose the transmission (fluid condition, TCC control, bulletins) rather than the engine.

outcomes.label: Could not reproduce the complaint
outcomes.interpretation: Ask the customer to demonstrate, or use a data logger over several drives.

tests.title: Check MAF plausibility at idle and wide-open throttle
tests.purpose: Confirm whether the MAF under-reports airflow.
procedure: Inspect the air filter and intake duct for contamination, oil, or unmetered air leaks after the MAF.
Record MAF airflow at warm idle and during a brief wide-open-throttle acceleration in a safe location.
Compare readings with known-good data for this engine or with an expected value from a volumetric efficiency calculation (general guideline — verify against OEM data).
Inspect the sensing element for contamination without touching it; clean only with a cleaner approved for MAF sensors, if the OEM permits.
tools: Known-good data or volumetric efficiency calculator
tests.expected: MAF airflow agrees with known-good data at idle and wide-open throttle.
tests.specNote: Expected airflow per OEM or known-good reference data.

outcomes.label: Airflow readings plausible
outcomes.interpretation: The MAF is reporting correctly.

outcomes.label: Airflow low compared with expected, especially at wide-open throttle
outcomes.interpretation: Either the MAF under-reports or the engine is truly breathing less (restriction). Check exhaust backpressure before replacing the MAF.

tests.title: Monitor fuel pressure during the stumble
tests.purpose: Determine whether supply pressure sags when demand rises.
procedure: Use the fuel pressure PID or connect a gauge or transducer to the low-pressure test port after relieving pressure per the OEM procedure, with fire precautions in place.
Never route a pressurized fuel hose into the passenger compartment; use a transducer and scope or an externally mounted gauge.
Record pressure at idle and during the acceleration that causes the complaint.
Relieve pressure, remove the equipment, and check for leaks.
tools: Fuel pressure gauge or transducer with lab scope
tests.expected: Pressure stays within the OEM specification during the acceleration.
tests.specNote: Fuel pressure specification per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Pressure holds during the stumble
outcomes.interpretation: Supply pressure is adequate.

outcomes.label: Pressure drops during the stumble
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose fuel delivery (pump, filter, regulator, and pump circuit voltage) before other components.

tests.title: Test coils and inspect plugs on the misfiring cylinders
tests.purpose: Confirm or rule out ignition breakdown under load.
procedure: Identify misfiring cylinders from the recorded misfire counters.
Engine off: remove coils and plugs; inspect plugs for wear, gap, and fouling, and coil boots for tracking or cracks.
Swap a suspect coil to another cylinder or view secondary ignition under load with a scope, and see whether the misfire follows.
Reinstall plugs tightened to the OEM specification.
tools: Spark plug socket and torque wrench
tests.expected: Plugs in serviceable condition and correctly gapped; misfire does not follow the coil.
tests.specNote: Plug type, gap, and tightening torque per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Coils and plugs good
outcomes.interpretation: Ignition is not the cause; check injectors and fuel delivery for the misfiring cylinders.

outcomes.label: Misfire follows the coil or weak secondary output
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the coil and inspect its boot and plug.

outcomes.label: Plugs worn, gapped wide, or fouled
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the plugs; investigate any fouling source.

tests.title: Smoke test the intake for vacuum leaks
tests.purpose: Locate unmetered air that leans the mixture at light load.
procedure: With the engine off, seal the intake at the air filter or MAF outlet per the smoke machine instructions.
Introduce smoke into the intake at the machine's intake test setting.
Inspect hoses, gaskets, the PCV system, the brake booster hose, and the intake duct after the MAF.
Remove the equipment and reconnect all hoses.
tests.expected: No smoke escapes.

outcomes.label: No smoke escapes
outcomes.interpretation: No intake leak.

outcomes.label: Smoke escapes from the intake, a hose, or the PCV system
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the leak and repeat the road test.

tests.title: Inspect the throttle plate for deposits
tests.purpose: Carbon at the plate edge causes a dead spot just off idle.
procedure: Key off; keep fingers out of electronic throttle bores whenever the key is on.
Remove the intake duct and inspect the plate edge and bore for deposits.
If deposits are heavy, clean per the OEM procedure (some bores are coated) and perform the throttle or idle relearn.
Repeat the tip-in road test.
tests.expected: Plate and bore free of significant deposits.

outcomes.label: No significant deposits
outcomes.interpretation: Throttle deposits are not the cause.

outcomes.label: Heavy deposits at the plate edge
outcomes.interpretation: Clean, relearn, and repeat the road test.

tests.title: Exhaust backpressure test
tests.purpose: Confirm or rule out a restricted converter or exhaust.
procedure: Allow the exhaust to cool before installing test equipment.
Install a backpressure gauge in the upstream oxygen sensor port (or the OEM-specified point).
Record backpressure at idle and at a steady elevated engine speed, and watch for a rise during a snap throttle.
Remove the gauge and reinstall the sensor with anti-seize if specified by the OEM.
tests.expected: Backpressure within the OEM specification.
tests.specNote: Backpressure limits per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Backpressure within specification
outcomes.interpretation: The exhaust is not restricted.

outcomes.label: Excessive backpressure
outcomes.interpretation: Locate the restriction and find why the converter failed (misfire, oil or coolant consumption) before replacing it.

tests.title: Determine whether the event is torque converter clutch shudder
tests.purpose: Separate TCC shudder from an engine stumble.
procedure: Record TCC command, TCC slip, engine RPM, and turbine speed during the light-throttle cruise that triggers the complaint.
Where supported, command the TCC off with the scan tool (or lightly touch the brake pedal to release the TCC on many vehicles) during the event and note whether the vibration stops.
Check transmission fluid level and condition per the OEM procedure.
Check bulletins for TCC shudder concerns.
tests.expected: No vibration change when the TCC is released, and stable TCC slip when applied.

outcomes.label: Event unaffected by releasing the TCC
outcomes.interpretation: The torque converter clutch is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Vibration stops when the TCC releases, or slip oscillates when applied
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose TCC control, fluid condition, and converter per the OEM procedure and bulletins.

tests.title: Injector flow and balance test
tests.purpose: Identify restricted injectors that lean the mixture under load.
procedure: Compare injector current waveforms across cylinders with a low-amp probe.
Port injection: perform an injector balance (pressure drop) test per the OEM procedure, relieving and restoring fuel pressure safely with fire precautions in place.
Direct injection: use OEM injector tests and cylinder contribution data only; do not open the high-pressure system.
Compare cylinder results with each other.
tools: Fuel pressure gauge and injector pulser (port injection)
tests.expected: Injector waveforms and flow consistent across cylinders.
tests.specNote: Allowable variation per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Injectors consistent
outcomes.interpretation: Injectors are not the cause.

outcomes.label: One or more injectors low flow or abnormal
outcomes.interpretation: Service or replace the affected injectors per the OEM procedure and repeat the road test.

tests.title: Check TSBs and calibration updates for hesitation concerns
tests.purpose: Drivability calibrations and TCC shudder bulletins are common for hesitation complaints.
procedure: Search the OEM service portal by VIN and symptom (hesitation, stumble, shudder).
Compare PCM and TCM calibration IDs with the latest releases.
Review bulletin conditions and required pre-checks.
tests.expected: No applicable bulletin, or the bulletin procedure is followed.

outcomes.label: Calibration update applies to this complaint
outcomes.interpretation: Confirm the hardware tests good, then reprogram per the bulletin and repeat the road test.

outcomes.label: Bulletin covers a component or service procedure
outcomes.interpretation: Follow the bulletin's confirmation steps before replacing parts.

outcomes.label: No applicable bulletin
outcomes.interpretation: Continue with standard diagnosis.

verification: Repeat the road test under the conditions that caused the complaint while recording data, and confirm no stumble, misfire counts, or lean excursions.
Confirm fuel pressure and fuel trims are normal under load.
If the torque converter clutch was involved, confirm smooth TCC apply with stable slip.
Confirm no pending codes after the drive.

playbooks.title: Hard start or long crank (engine eventually starts)
playbooks.summary: A long crank at normal cranking speed means the engine is missing fuel pressure, crank/cam synchronization, or the correct start-up mixture. First classify the complaint (cold, hot, after refueling, or slow cranking) and check cranking speed, the RPM signal while cranking, and coolant temperature plausibility. Then test fuel pressure build-up and leak-down, isolate any leak-down path, and check purge valve sealing and ignition before replacing parts.
clarifyingQuestions: Does the engine crank at normal speed, or does it crank slowly?
Is it hard to start cold (first start of the day), hot (after a short stop), or only after refueling?
Does it start normally if the key is cycled on and off a few times before cranking, or with the accelerator pressed slightly?
Once started, does it run rough, smoke, or smell of fuel?
Does the tachometer move while cranking, and are any codes stored or pending?

causes.title: Weak fuel pump or leaking pump check valve
causes.description: A leaking check valve lets pressure drain back to the tank after shutdown, so the pump must rebuild pressure while cranking; a weak pump builds pressure slowly.

modifiers.reason: Long crank after the vehicle sits
Fuel pressure or pump circuit code present

causes.title: Leaking fuel pressure regulator
causes.description: A leaking regulator bleeds rail pressure after shutdown and, if its diaphragm is ruptured, can pull fuel into the intake and cause a rich, flooded start.

causes.title: Leaking fuel injector
causes.description: An injector that drips after shutdown floods one cylinder and drains rail pressure, causing long cranks, especially on hot restarts, with a puff of smoke or a rough first few seconds.

causes.title: Coolant temperature sensor reading incorrectly
causes.description: The PCM sets cranking fuel from coolant temperature; a sensor reading hot on a cold engine starves the start, and one reading cold on a hot engine floods it.

modifiers.reason: Coolant temperature or thermostat code present

causes.title: Weak or intermittent crankshaft position signal
causes.description: A weak or late crank signal delays synchronization, so the PCM cannot fire injectors or coils until cranking speed or sensor temperature changes.

modifiers.reason: Crank/cam correlation or cam sensor code present

causes.title: Weak battery (slow cranking)
causes.description: Low cranking speed and voltage reduce crank signal strength, injector and coil output, and module operation, so the engine takes longer to start.

modifiers.reason: Battery capacity drops in the cold

causes.title: Purge valve stuck open (hard start after refueling)
causes.description: A purge valve that leaks when closed lets fuel vapor from a freshly filled tank flood the intake, causing a long crank and rough start right after refueling.

causes.title: Worn or fouled spark plugs
causes.description: Worn or fuel-fouled plugs need more voltage than the ignition provides during cranking, especially cold or in damp weather.

modifiers.reason: Plugs may be past their service interval

causes.title: Large vacuum leak
causes.description: A large leak leans the start-up mixture and can prevent the engine from catching until the throttle is opened or the PCM adapts.

causes.title: Insufficient idle air (carbon-restricted throttle or idle passage)
causes.description: When idle air is restricted, the engine may only start with the pedal slightly pressed, and may stall right after starting.

modifiers.match: pedal|press(ing)? the gas|starts then dies|dies after start
modifiers.reason: Needs pedal to start or stalls after starting

tests.title: Check cranking speed, RPM signal while cranking, and coolant temperature plausibility
tests.purpose: Quickly separate slow cranking, missing crank synchronization, and coolant temperature errors from fuel, ignition, and air problems.
procedure: Check for stored and pending codes in all modules.
After an overnight cold soak, read coolant and intake air temperature at key on; they should be close to each other and to ambient (compare against OEM guidance).
While cranking, record battery voltage, cranking RPM, and whether the RPM PID (or tachometer) shows a steady signal; note the time until the engine fires.
Repeat on a hot restart if that is the complaint.
tests.expected: Normal cranking speed and voltage, a steady RPM signal from the start of cranking, and coolant temperature plausible for conditions.
tests.specNote: Cranking voltage and speed expectations per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Cranking speed, RPM signal, and temperatures all normal
outcomes.interpretation: Focus on fuel pressure, leak-down, purge, ignition, and air.

outcomes.label: Cranking speed or voltage low
outcomes.interpretation: Test the battery, cables, and starter before diagnosing fuel or ignition.

outcomes.label: RPM signal absent, delayed, or erratic while cranking
outcomes.interpretation: Test the crankshaft position sensor signal and wiring while cranking.

outcomes.label: Coolant temperature implausible (disagrees with intake air after a soak, or with actual temperature)
outcomes.interpretation: Test the coolant temperature sensor and circuit.

tests.title: Start after cycling the key to prime, and with the pedal slightly pressed
tests.purpose: A quick no-tool test that points toward pressure leak-down or insufficient idle air.
procedure: After the vehicle has sat long enough to produce the complaint, cycle the key on (engine off) several times, pausing for the pump prime each time, then start; note whether the long crank disappears.
On another occasion under the same conditions, start with the accelerator pressed only slightly; do not floor the pedal unless intending clear-flood mode.
Note which method, if any, makes the engine start normally.
tests.expected: No difference: the engine starts promptly without either aid.

outcomes.label: Priming by cycling the key eliminates the long crank
outcomes.interpretation: Fuel pressure is bleeding down after shutdown; test leak-down and isolate the path.

outcomes.label: A slightly open throttle makes it start normally
outcomes.interpretation: Idle airflow is insufficient or the start-up mixture is rich; inspect the throttle and idle air passage, and check for flooding sources.

outcomes.label: Neither method changes the start
outcomes.interpretation: Leak-down and idle air are less likely; check sync, ignition, and sensor inputs.

tests.title: Fuel pressure build-up at prime and hold after shutdown
tests.purpose: Measure whether pressure builds quickly and whether it bleeds down after shutdown.
procedure: Use the fuel pressure PID, or relieve pressure per the OEM procedure and connect a gauge to the low-pressure test port with fire precautions in place (direct injection: low-pressure side only).
Key on: record how quickly pressure builds during prime and the value reached.
Run the engine, shut it off, and record pressure hold over the time specified by the OEM (or leave the gauge connected overnight where safe).
Relieve pressure, remove the gauge, and check for leaks.
tests.expected: Pressure builds promptly to the OEM specification and holds for the specified time after shutdown.
tests.specNote: Prime pressure and hold specification per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Pressure builds promptly and holds
outcomes.interpretation: Fuel supply is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Pressure slow to build or low at prime
outcomes.interpretation: Check pump voltage under load and pump output; see the fuel pressure diagnostics.

outcomes.label: Pressure builds normally but bleeds down after shutdown
outcomes.interpretation: Isolate the leak path: pump check valve, regulator, or injector.

tests.title: Isolate the fuel pressure leak-down path
tests.purpose: Identify whether pressure is lost through the pump check valve, the regulator, or an injector.
procedure: Relieve pressure per the OEM procedure; observe fire precautions (extinguisher, ventilation, no ignition sources, eye protection).

Using gauge adapters with shutoff valves or OEM-approved line blocking tools (do not pinch nylon or metal fuel lines), pressurize the rail and close the supply side; if pressure now holds, the pump check valve is leaking.
On return-type systems, block the return side; if pressure then holds, the regulator is leaking. Check the regulator vacuum hose for fuel.
If pressure still drops with supply and return blocked, an injector is leaking; identify it with the OEM method (for example, a fuel-wet plug or cylinder-specific misfire on restart).
Restore all connections and check for leaks with the system pressurized.
tools: Fuel pressure gauge with shutoff valves
tests.expected: Pressure holds with no identifiable leak path.
tests.specNote: Blocking method and hold time per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Pressure holds; no leak path found
outcomes.interpretation: Leak-down is not present; revisit prime pressure and other causes.

outcomes.label: Holds when the supply side is blocked (pump check valve leaking)
outcomes.interpretation: The pump check valve is leaking; it is usually serviced with the pump or module.

outcomes.label: Holds when the return side is blocked, or fuel found in the regulator vacuum hose
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the regulator and check plugs and oil for fuel contamination.

outcomes.label: Drops even with supply and return blocked (injector leaking)
outcomes.interpretation: Identify and replace the leaking injector; check that cylinder for fuel-washed walls and the oil for dilution.

tests.title: Scope the crankshaft position signal while cranking
tests.purpose: Confirm the crank signal is strong and clean from the first revolution.
procedure: Back-probe the crankshaft position sensor signal (and supply and ground for active sensors).
Capture the signal on a lab scope while cranking, cold and hot if the complaint is temperature related.
Look for low amplitude, missing teeth pattern errors, dropouts, or noise; compare with known-good data.
Inspect the sensor for metallic debris and correct seating if the signal is weak.
tests.expected: A clean, regular signal with the correct reference pattern from the start of cranking.
tests.specNote: Signal pattern and supply values per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Signal clean and strong
outcomes.interpretation: The crank signal is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Low amplitude, dropouts, or noise
outcomes.interpretation: Check sensor seating, debris, air gap, wiring, and the reluctor before replacing the sensor.

outcomes.label: No signal or missing supply or ground
outcomes.interpretation: Test the sensor circuit; if the circuit is good, the sensor is faulty.

tests.title: Verify coolant temperature sensor accuracy
tests.purpose: Confirm the PCM receives the correct engine temperature for cranking fuel.
procedure: After a cold soak, compare the coolant temperature PID with intake air temperature and ambient temperature.
Warm the engine and compare the PID with the actual temperature measured at the sensor location with an infrared thermometer or contact probe.
If readings disagree, check sensor resistance against the OEM temperature chart and inspect the connector and wiring.
Check coolant level; an air pocket around the sensor causes false readings.
tests.expected: Coolant temperature PID agrees with actual temperature across the warm-up.
tests.specNote: Resistance versus temperature values per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Reading accurate
outcomes.interpretation: The coolant temperature input is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Reading skewed, or circuit fault found
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the circuit or replace the sensor, bleed the cooling system if needed, and retest a cold start.

tests.title: Battery and cranking system test
tests.purpose: Confirm or rule out a weak battery as the reason for slow cranking.
procedure: Check the battery state of charge and test it with a conductance or load tester per the tester instructions.
Clean and tighten battery terminals and check main cables and grounds for corrosion.
Measure cranking voltage at the battery and voltage drop across the positive and negative cranking circuits.
Wear eye protection and avoid shorting across battery terminals.
tests.expected: Battery passes the test and cranking voltage and circuit voltage drops are within OEM guidance.
tests.specNote: Battery rating, cranking voltage, and voltage drop limits per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Battery and cranking circuit good
outcomes.interpretation: The battery is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Battery fails the test or discharged
outcomes.interpretation: Charge and retest; replace if it fails, then check charging output and parasitic draw.

outcomes.label: Battery good but cranking voltage drop or slow cranking persists
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the starter and cranking circuit.

tests.title: Check the purge valve for leakage (hard start after refueling)
tests.purpose: Confirm whether fuel vapor is entering the intake through a purge valve that does not seal.
procedure: With the engine off, disconnect the canister-side hose at the purge valve.
Apply vacuum with a hand pump; a normally closed valve should hold.
Inspect the valve ports and canister line for charcoal granules or liquid fuel.
Reconnect the hose.
tests.expected: The purge valve holds vacuum when not energized.

outcomes.label: Purge valve holds vacuum
outcomes.interpretation: The purge valve is not flooding the intake.

outcomes.label: Purge valve leaks when closed
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the purge valve and inspect the canister for liquid fuel or charcoal.

tests.title: Check spark while cranking and inspect spark plugs
tests.purpose: Confirm adequate spark at cranking speed and plugs in good condition.
procedure: Disable fuel injection per the OEM procedure, or use an adjustable spark tester that does not create an open spark near fuel vapor.
Check for strong, consistent spark on each cylinder while cranking.
Remove and inspect plugs for wear, gap, and fuel, oil, or carbon fouling.
Reinstall plugs tightened to the OEM specification and restore fuel injection.
tools: Spark plug socket and torque wrench
tests.expected: Strong spark on all cylinders and plugs in serviceable condition.
tests.specNote: Plug type, gap, and tightening torque per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Spark strong and plugs good
outcomes.interpretation: Ignition is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Weak or missing spark on one or more cylinders
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the ignition coil and its circuit on those cylinders.

outcomes.label: Plugs worn, fuel-fouled, or oil-fouled
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the plugs and find the cause of any fouling (for example a leaking injector on a fuel-wet cylinder).

tests.title: Check TSBs and recalls for hard-start concerns
tests.purpose: Fuel pump check valve, injector, and cold- or hot-start calibration bulletins are common.
procedure: Search the OEM service portal by VIN and symptom (long crank, hard start cold or hot).
Check open recalls for fuel pumps and pump modules.
Compare the PCM calibration ID with the latest release.
tests.expected: No applicable bulletin, or the bulletin procedure is followed.

outcomes.label: Recall or bulletin for the fuel pump or check valve, injectors, regulator, or purge valve
outcomes.interpretation: Follow the bulletin's diagnostic steps to confirm the condition before replacing parts; recalls must be performed by an authorized dealer.

outcomes.label: Bulletin or calibration for cold or hot start, crank or temperature sensing, or idle air
outcomes.interpretation: Verify the bulletin condition, then perform the specified repair or reprogramming and retest cold and hot starts.

outcomes.label: No applicable bulletin or recall
outcomes.interpretation: Continue with standard diagnosis.

verification: Confirm prompt starts cold (after an overnight soak), hot (after a short heat soak), and after refueling if that was the complaint.
Confirm fuel pressure builds at prime and holds for the OEM-specified time after shutdown.
Confirm cranking speed and the RPM signal are normal during cranking.
Confirm no pending codes and a stable idle after starting.

playbooks.title: Engine stalls or dies
playbooks.summary: Stalling is diagnosed by capturing what drops first when the engine dies: the crank RPM signal, fuel pressure or pump power, system or PCM voltage, or idle speed as the vehicle comes to a stop (including a torque converter clutch that does not release). Classify the stall with freeze frame data and a data logger, then run the targeted test for that path before replacing parts. Reproduce stalls only in a safe location, never in traffic, because power steering and brake assist are reduced when the engine stops.
clarifyingQuestions: Does it stall when coming to a stop, at idle, while driving at speed, or right after starting?
When it stalls, do the dash lights and gauges stay on, and does the tachometer drop to zero before the engine dies?
Does it restart immediately, or only after cooling down for a while?
Is it worse hot or cold, with the A/C on, or when shifting into gear?
Is the battery or charging warning light on, or have there been other electrical problems?

causes.title: Insufficient idle airflow (carbon-restricted throttle or idle passage)
causes.description: Carbon restricts idle airflow so RPM sags and the engine dies when coming to a stop or when loads such as A/C come on.

modifiers.reason: Stalls at idle or when stopping
Idle control or low idle code present

causes.title: Fuel pump cutting out or losing output
causes.description: A failing pump can stop intermittently (worn commutator dead spots) or lose output when hot, so the engine dies while driving and may restart after cooling.

modifiers.reason: Stalls while driving or when hot
Fuel pressure or pump circuit code present

causes.title: Crankshaft position sensor dropping out (often when hot)
causes.description: A sensor with an internal fault loses its signal as it heats up; the tachometer drops to zero, the engine dies, and it often will not restart until it cools.

modifiers.reason: Cam sensor or correlation code present

causes.title: Large vacuum leak
causes.description: A large leak leans the idle mixture and destabilizes idle control, so the engine stalls at idle or right after starting.

modifiers.reason: Lean or high idle code present

causes.title: Contaminated or faulty mass airflow sensor
causes.description: Incorrect airflow readings at low flow miscalculate fuel on deceleration and at idle, causing stalls when coming to a stop or just after starting.

modifiers.reason: Stall after start or on deceleration

causes.title: EGR valve stuck open
causes.description: Exhaust gas admitted at idle dilutes the mixture enough to stall the engine at stops.

modifiers.reason: Stalls at idle or when stopping

causes.title: Torque converter clutch not releasing
causes.description: If the torque converter clutch stays applied as the vehicle slows, the engine is dragged down and stalls at stops, much like a manual transmission with the clutch engaged.

modifiers.match: coming to a stop|in gear|into (drive|reverse)|put(ting)? it in gear|shift
modifiers.reason: Stalls when stopping in gear or on engagement

causes.title: Intermittent fuel pump relay or pump power circuit
causes.description: Burned relay contacts or an intermittent pump feed cut the pump without warning; the engine dies while driving and often restarts right away.

causes.title: PCM power or ignition feed interruption (ignition switch, main relay, or ground)
causes.description: A momentary loss of PCM power or ground, from a worn ignition switch, main relay, or loose ground, shuts the engine off; the dash may flicker and other modules may log communication codes.

causes.title: Charging system failure (engine dies as the battery drains)
causes.description: When the alternator stops charging, the vehicle runs on the battery until voltage is too low for ignition and injection; the engine dies while driving after electrical symptoms appear.

modifiers.reason: System voltage or generator control code present

tests.title: Capture the stall with freeze frame data and a data logger
tests.purpose: Identify what drops first when the engine dies: RPM signal, fuel supply, voltage, idle speed, or torque converter clutch release.
procedure: Check all modules for stored, pending, and history codes; review freeze frame data for any stall-related code.
Set up recording of RPM, desired and actual idle, idle airflow or throttle command, fuel pressure or pump command, system voltage and PCM supply voltage, MAF, EGR command, and TCC command and slip.
Reproduce the stall in a safe location (not in traffic), or give the customer a data logger to capture it.
Review the recording just before the stall to see which signal changed first.
tools: Scan tool with recording or a data logger
tests.expected: No stall occurs; RPM, fuel pressure, voltage, and idle speed stay stable and the TCC releases before stops.

outcomes.label: RPM signal drops to zero abruptly with everything else normal
outcomes.interpretation: Loss of crank signal is shutting the engine down; test the crank sensor and wiring, especially hot.

outcomes.label: Fuel pressure or pump command or power drops before the stall
outcomes.interpretation: Test the fuel pump and its power circuit (relay or pump control module, wiring, and grounds).

outcomes.label: System or PCM supply voltage drops before the stall
outcomes.interpretation: Test the charging system and the PCM power, ignition feed, and ground circuits.

outcomes.label: Idle speed sags below desired as the vehicle stops or when loads come on
outcomes.interpretation: Idle air or mixture is the problem: check throttle deposits, vacuum leaks, MAF readings, and EGR at idle.

outcomes.label: TCC remains applied as the vehicle slows to a stop
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose TCC control (solenoid, circuit, valve body, and fluid) per the OEM transmission procedure.

outcomes.label: Stall could not be captured
outcomes.interpretation: Use a data logger over several days or reproduce under the customer's exact conditions.

tests.title: Check battery condition and charging output
tests.purpose: Rule out an engine that dies because the charging system has stopped charging.
procedure: Test the battery with a conductance or load tester.
With the engine running, measure charging voltage at the battery at idle and with electrical loads on.
Check the generator warning lamp operation and any charging system codes in the PCM or body modules.
Inspect the drive belt and the generator connections.
tests.expected: Battery passes and charging voltage is within the OEM specification with and without loads.
tests.specNote: Charging voltage range per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Battery and charging output good
outcomes.interpretation: The charging system is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Low or no charging output
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the charging system (generator, belt, wiring, and control) before other stall causes.

tests.title: Monitor fuel pump power and fuel pressure during a road test
tests.purpose: Catch a pump or pump circuit that cuts out.
procedure: Connect a low-amp current probe on the pump feed (or a test light rated for the circuit) routed so it can be watched safely from inside the vehicle; never bring a pressurized fuel hose into the cabin.
Monitor fuel pressure through the PID or an externally mounted transducer.
Road test under the stall conditions with a helper, and tap the relay and flex the harness at the relay and tank connector (vehicle stopped, engine running).
Note whether pump current or pressure drops out or sags.
tools: Lab scope with low-amp current probe
tests.expected: Pump current and fuel pressure remain steady throughout.

outcomes.label: Pump current and pressure steady
outcomes.interpretation: Fuel delivery did not cause the stall during this test.

outcomes.label: Pump current drops out (with or without tapping or flexing)
outcomes.interpretation: If power at the pump drops out, repair the relay or circuit; if power stays but current stops, the pump has a dead spot.

outcomes.label: Pump runs but pressure sags
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose pump output, restriction, and regulator; see the fuel pressure diagnostics.

tests.title: Monitor the crank signal when the engine is hot
tests.purpose: Confirm a crank sensor that drops out as it heats up.
procedure: Warm the engine fully, or heat-soak it after a drive.
Monitor the crank signal on a lab scope and the RPM PID at idle and during light acceleration in the shop.
If the OEM permits, gently warm the sensor with a heat gun on low setting while monitoring; keep heat away from fuel lines, wiring insulation, and plastic components.
Wiggle the sensor harness while monitoring.
tests.expected: The crank signal remains clean and stable when hot and while the harness is flexed.

outcomes.label: Signal stable when hot
outcomes.interpretation: The crank sensor is unlikely to be the cause.

outcomes.label: Signal weakens or drops out when hot or when the harness is flexed
outcomes.interpretation: Check the connector and wiring, then replace the sensor if the fault is internal.

tests.title: Inspect the throttle body and idle airflow values
tests.purpose: Confirm or rule out restricted idle airflow.
procedure: Review the idle airflow learn value or IAC position at warm idle; a value near its limit suggests restriction.
Key off (keep fingers out of electronic throttle bores whenever the key is on) and inspect the throttle plate and bore for carbon.
If deposits are heavy, clean per the OEM procedure (some bores are coated) and perform the idle relearn.
Recheck idle stability coming to a stop with loads on.
tests.expected: Idle airflow values within normal range and throttle free of significant deposits.
tests.specNote: Normal idle airflow learn range per OEM service information.

outcomes.label: Throttle clean and idle airflow normal
outcomes.interpretation: Idle air restriction is unlikely.

outcomes.label: Heavy deposits or idle airflow at its limit
outcomes.interpretation: Clean, relearn, and retest stops with loads on.

tests.title: Smoke test the intake for vacuum leaks
tests.purpose: Locate a large unmetered air leak.
procedure: With the engine off, seal the intake at the air filter or MAF outlet per the smoke machine instructions.
Introduce smoke into the intake at the machine's intake test setting.
Inspect hoses, gaskets, the PCV system, and the brake booster hose and check valve.
Remove the equipment and reconnect all hoses.
tests.expected: No smoke escapes.

outcomes.label: No smoke escapes
outcomes.interpretation: No significant intake leak.

outcomes.label: Smoke escapes from the intake, a hose, or the PCV system
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the leak and retest idle stability.

tests.title: Check MAF readings at idle and during deceleration
tests.purpose: Confirm whether incorrect airflow readings cause stalls at stops or after starting.
procedure: Inspect the air filter and intake duct for contamination and leaks after the MAF.
Compare MAF airflow at warm idle with known-good data for this engine, and watch the reading during deceleration to a stop.
Inspect the sensing element for contamination; clean only with a MAF-safe cleaner if the OEM permits.
Use unplugging the MAF (engine behavior on default airflow) only as a supporting check, not as proof.
tests.expected: MAF readings agree with known-good data and change smoothly during deceleration.
tests.specNote: Expected airflow per OEM or known-good reference data.

outcomes.label: MAF readings plausible
outcomes.interpretation: The MAF is not the cause.

outcomes.label: MAF readings low, erratic, or slow to respond
outcomes.interpretation: Rule out air leaks after the MAF, then clean or replace the MAF and retest.

tests.title: Check for EGR flow at idle
tests.purpose: Determine whether a stuck-open EGR valve causes stalls at stops.
procedure: At warm idle, confirm EGR is commanded closed and, where available, that the position PID reads closed.
Temporarily block EGR flow per the OEM procedure (or disconnect the valve where permitted) and note whether idle stabilizes.
Restore the system and clear any codes set by the test.
tools: Block-off plate or OEM tool as specified
tests.expected: No change in idle when EGR flow is blocked.

outcomes.label: Idle unchanged with EGR blocked
outcomes.interpretation: EGR is not flowing at idle.

outcomes.label: Idle stabilizes with EGR blocked
outcomes.interpretation: The EGR valve is stuck or leaking open; inspect and clean or replace it.

outcomes.label: Engine has no external EGR valve
outcomes.interpretation: Not applicable.

tests.title: Verify the torque converter clutch releases when stopping
tests.purpose: Confirm whether the TCC stays applied and drags the engine down.
procedure: Record TCC command, TCC slip, engine RPM, and vehicle speed while decelerating to a stop on a safe road.
Note whether TCC slip stays near zero (applied) as speed falls and RPM is pulled down with road speed.
If it does, check whether the command is off while the clutch stays applied (hydraulic or mechanical) or the command itself stays on (electrical or control).
Check transmission fluid level and condition per the OEM procedure.
tests.expected: The TCC releases well before the vehicle stops, and engine RPM returns to idle.

outcomes.label: TCC releases normally
outcomes.interpretation: The TCC is not causing the stall.

outcomes.label: TCC stays applied and pulls RPM down
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the TCC solenoid, its circuit, the valve body, and the fluid per the OEM procedure.

tests.title: PCM power, ignition feed, and ground wiggle and voltage drop test
tests.purpose: Find an intermittent loss of PCM power or ground that shuts the engine off.
procedure: Monitor PCM supply voltage (PID or back-probed) and RPM with the engine idling.
Gently wiggle the ignition switch and key (where applicable), the main relay, PCM connectors, and engine and body grounds.
Perform voltage drop tests on PCM power and ground circuits under load.
Note any dropout, stall, or dash flicker and its location.
tests.expected: PCM supply voltage stays steady and voltage drops are small (general guideline: a few tenths of a volt or less — verify against OEM specification).

outcomes.label: PCM power and ground stable
outcomes.interpretation: PCM power supply is not the cause.

outcomes.label: PCM power or ground drops out or shows excessive voltage drop
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the ignition switch, relay, connector, or ground at the location found, and retest.

tests.title: Check TSBs and recalls for stalling concerns
tests.purpose: Stall-at-stop calibrations, ignition switch recalls, and fuel pump recalls are common.
procedure: Search the OEM service portal by VIN and symptom (stall at stop, stall while driving, stall after start).
Check open recalls, particularly for fuel pumps and ignition switches.
Compare PCM and TCM calibration IDs with the latest releases.
tests.expected: No applicable recall or bulletin, or the bulletin procedure is followed.

outcomes.label: Recall or bulletin for the fuel pump, pump relay or module, ignition switch, crank sensor, or charging system
outcomes.interpretation: Follow the bulletin's diagnostic steps to confirm the condition before replacing parts; recalls must be performed by an authorized dealer.

outcomes.label: Bulletin or calibration for stall-at-stop, idle airflow, MAF, EGR, or torque converter clutch control
outcomes.interpretation: Confirm the bulletin condition (for example with the event data capture), then perform the specified repair or reprogramming.

outcomes.label: No applicable bulletin or recall
outcomes.interpretation: Continue with standard diagnosis.

verification: Drive through the conditions that caused the stall (stops, idle with loads, hot restarts, highway) with data logging, and confirm no stall.
Confirm idle stays at the desired speed with the A/C on, with gear engagement, and when coming to a stop.
Confirm fuel pressure, system voltage, and the RPM signal remain stable throughout the drive.
Confirm no pending codes after the drive.
